sentences.zh: 毛澄，字憲清，昆山人。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng, styled Xianqing, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng, styled Xianqing, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治六年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he placed first among metropolitan graduates.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 6 he took first place in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 預修《會典》成，進右諭德，直講東宮。

translations.literal: When the Statutes Compilation, in which he had taken part, was completed, he was promoted to Right Tutor and lectured in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After helping compile the Statutes and seeing that work finished, he was promoted to Right Tutor and lectured in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 武宗為太子，以澄進講明晰稱之帝。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was crown prince, because Cheng's lectures were clear, [the prince] praised him to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong was still crown prince, he praised Cheng's lucid lectures to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 方秋夜置宴，即徹以賜。

translations.literal: It was just an autumn evening banquet; [the emperor] immediately had it cleared and bestowed it upon him.
translations.idiomatic: It was an autumn evening feast; the emperor at once had the banquet cleared and sent it to Cheng as a gift.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，進左庶子，直經筵。

translations.literal: When Wuzong acceded, [Cheng] was promoted to Left Household Superintendent and attended the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, Cheng was promoted to Left Household Superintendent and served at the Classics Lectern.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，劉瑾摘《會典》小疵貶諸纂修者秩，以澄為侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde, Liu Jin seized on minor flaws in the Statutes to demote the compilers' ranks; Cheng was made Court Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 4 Liu Jin found petty faults in the Statutes and used them to demote the compilers; Cheng was reduced to Court Reader.

sentences.zh: 服闋還朝，進侍講學士。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed he returned to court and was promoted to Bachelor of Exposition.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he returned to court and was promoted to Hanlin Bachelor of Exposition.

sentences.zh: 再遷學士，掌院事，歷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Bachelor, took charge of Hanlin affairs, and served as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Bachelor, directed Hanlin affairs, and eventually served as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月拜尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was appointed Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Zhengde he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其年八月朔，帝微行。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month that year, the emperor went out incognito.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month that year the emperor slipped out of the palace incognito.

sentences.zh: 澄率侍郎王瓚、顧清等疏請還宮。

translations.literal: Cheng led Vice Ministers Wang Zan, Gu Qing, and others in a memorial asking him to return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng led Vice Ministers Wang Zan, Gu Qing, and others in memorials urging him to return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 既又出居庸，幸宣府，久留不返。

translations.literal: He then went out through Juyong Pass, visited Xuanfu, and remained away for a long time without returning.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed through Juyong Pass, traveled to Xuanfu, and stayed away for a long time without coming back.

sentences.zh: 澄等頻疏諫，悉不報。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others remonstrated repeatedly by memorial; none received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and his colleagues remonstrated again and again; none of their memorials was answered.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，駕旋，命百官戎服郊迎。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the imperial carriage returned, and the emperor ordered all officials to greet him outside the city in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the emperor returned, and he ordered all officials to greet him outside the city in military dress.

sentences.zh: 澄等請用常服，不許。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others asked that ordinary dress be used; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and the others asked to wear ordinary court dress instead; the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝自稱威武大將軍朱壽，統六師巡邊。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor styled himself the Martially Awesome Grand General Zhu Shou and led six armies on a border tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor took the title Martially Awesome Grand General Zhu Shou and led six armies on a tour of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遂幸宣府，抵大同，歷山西至榆林。

translations.literal: He then visited Xuanfu, reached Datong, and traveled through Shanxi as far as Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to Xuanfu, reached Datong, and traveled through Shanxi as far as Yulin.

sentences.zh: 澄等屢疏馳諫。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others repeatedly sent urgent memorials of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and his colleagues sent urgent memorial after memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 至十二月，復偕廷臣上疏曰：「去歲正月以來，鑾輿數駕，不遑寧居。

translations.literal: By the twelfth month they again joined court officials in a memorial saying: "Since the first month of last year the imperial carriage has set out many times, and Your Majesty has had no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they again joined the court in a memorial: "Since the first month of last year Your Majesty's carriage has been on the road again and again, with no time to rest.

sentences.zh: 今茲之行，又已半歲。

translations.literal: This present journey has already lasted half a year.
translations.idiomatic: This present journey has already lasted half a year.

sentences.zh: 宗廟、社稷享祀之禮並系攝行，萬壽、正旦、冬至朝賀之儀悉從簡略。

translations.literal: The rites of offering at the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain have all been performed by proxy; the ceremonies of court congratulations on the imperial birthday, New Year's Day, and the winter solstice have all been simplified.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain have all been carried out by deputies; birthday, New Year, and winter-solstice audiences have all been curtailed.

sentences.zh: 臘朔省牲，闕而不行，遂二年矣。

translations.literal: The inspection of sacrificial animals at the twelfth-month new moon has been omitted and not performed; this has now gone on for two years.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth-month inspection of sacrificial victims has been skipped for two years running.

sentences.zh: 歲律將周，郊禋已卜。

translations.literal: The year is about to turn full circle, and the suburban sacrifice has already been divined.
translations.idiomatic: The year is nearly complete, and the date for the suburban sacrifice has already been chosen.

sentences.zh: 皇祖之訓曰：『凡祀天地，精誠則感格，怠慢則禍生。』

translations.literal: Our imperial ancestor's instruction says: 'In all sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, sincerity brings response, and negligence brings calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperor taught: 'In all sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, sincerity wins response, and negligence brings disaster.

sentences.zh: 今六龍遐騁，旋軫無日。

translations.literal: Now the six dragons race far away, and the day of turning the carriage wheel homeward is nowhere in sight.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial carriage races far away, and there is no day in sight for its return.

sentences.zh: 萬一冰雪阻違，道途梗塞，元正上日不及躬執玉帛於上帝前，陛下何以自安？

translations.literal: If by chance ice and snow block the way and the roads are cut off, so that on the supreme day of the New Year Your Majesty cannot in person hold jade and silk before the Supreme Lord, how can Your Majesty be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: If ice and snow should block the roads, and on New Year's Day Your Majesty cannot in person present jade and silk before Heaven, how will Your Majesty be at ease?

sentences.zh: 且邊地荒寒，隆冬尤甚。

translations.literal: Moreover, the borderlands are desolate and cold, and deep winter is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the frontier is bleak and cold, and deep winter there is especially harsh.

sentences.zh: 臣等處重城，食厚祿，仰思聖體勞頓，根本空虛，遙望清塵，憂心如醉。

translations.literal: We your subjects dwell within the great city and eat generous stipends; looking up we think of the sacred person wearied and exhausted, the root of the state left empty, and gazing from afar at the imperial dust our hearts are troubled as if drunk.
translations.idiomatic: We who remain in the capital on generous stipends think of Your Majesty worn out on the road and the state left without its foundation; gazing after your distant train, our hearts are sick with worry.

sentences.zh: 伏祈趣駕速還，躬親祼享，宗社臣民幸甚。」

translations.literal: We humbly pray that Your Majesty hasten the carriage and return quickly, and in person perform the libation and offering; the altars of state and the people would be greatly blessed."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to hurry home and perform the libation sacrifice in person; the altars of state and all your subjects would be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月，駕甫還京，即諭禮部：「總督軍務威武大將軍、總兵官、太師、鎮國公朱壽遣往兩畿，瞻東嶽，奉安聖像，祈福安民。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year, as soon as the imperial carriage had returned to the capital, an order was sent to the Ministry of Rites: "The Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs, Martially Awesome Grand General, Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, and Defender of the State Zhu Shou is dispatched to the two capitals regions to gaze upon the Eastern Peak, install the sacred image, and pray for blessings and the peace of the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourteenth year, as soon as the emperor returned to the capital, he instructed the Ministry of Rites: "Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs, Martially Awesome Grand General, Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, and Defender of the State Zhu Shou is to go to the two metropolitan regions, visit the Eastern Peak, install the sacred image, and pray for blessings and the people's welfare."

sentences.zh: 澄等駭愕，復偕廷臣上言：「陛下以天地之子，承祖宗之業，九州四海但知陛下有皇帝之號。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others were appalled and again joined court officials in a memorial: "Your Majesty, as son of Heaven and Earth, inherits the enterprise of the ancestors; throughout the nine provinces and four seas all know only that Your Majesty bears the title of emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and his colleagues were shocked and again joined the court in a memorial: "Your Majesty, as Son of Heaven, inherits the ancestral enterprise; throughout the realm everyone knows only that Your Majesty is emperor.

sentences.zh: 今曰『總督軍務、威武大將軍、太師、鎮國公』者，臣等莫知所指。

translations.literal: Now when it is said 'Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs, Martially Awesome Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Defender of the State,' we your subjects do not know to whom this refers.
translations.idiomatic: When the titles 'Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs, Martially Awesome Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Defender of the State' are used, we do not know who is meant.

sentences.zh: 夫出此旨者，陛下也。

translations.literal: The one who issued this decree is Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The one who issued this decree is Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 加此號者，陛下也。

translations.literal: The one who bestowed these titles is Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The one who bestowed these titles is Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 不知受此號者何人？

translations.literal: We do not know who receives these titles.
translations.idiomatic: Yet who is it that receives them?

sentences.zh: 如以皇儲未建，欲遍告名山大川，用祈默相，則遣使走幣，足將敬矣。

translations.literal: If because the heir apparent has not yet been established Your Majesty wishes to announce this to every famous mountain and great river and pray for silent assistance, then sending envoys with offerings would be sufficient to show reverence.
translations.idiomatic: If, because no heir has been named, Your Majesty wishes to announce this to every famous mountain and river and pray for Heaven's hidden aid, sending envoys with offerings would be reverence enough.

sentences.zh: 何必躬奉神像，獻寶香，如佛、老所為哉？」

translations.literal: Why must Your Majesty in person carry the sacred image and offer precious incense, as Buddhists and Daoists do?"
translations.idiomatic: Why must Your Majesty personally carry the sacred image and burn precious incense, as Buddhists and Daoists do?"

sentences.zh: 因歷陳五不可。

translations.literal: They then set forth in detail five reasons why this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: They then listed five reasons why this should not be done.

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: Again there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反江西，帝南征示威武，駐蹕留都者逾歲。

translations.literal: Chen Hao rebelled in Jiangxi; the emperor marched south to display martial might and halted his progress at the southern capital for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Ning Chen Hao rebelled in Jiangxi, the emperor marched south to display his military power and stayed at the southern capital for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 澄屢請回鑾。

translations.literal: Cheng repeatedly asked that the imperial carriage return.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng repeatedly urged the emperor to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及駕返通州，用江彬言，將即賜宸濠死。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Tongzhou, following Jiang Bin's advice [the emperor] was about to have Chen Hao put to death at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Tongzhou on his return, he followed Jiang Bin's advice and was about to have Chen Hao executed immediately.

sentences.zh: 澄據漢庶人故事，請還京告郊廟，獻俘行戮。

translations.literal: Cheng, citing the Han precedent regarding a deposed commoner, asked that [the emperor] return to the capital, announce victory at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, present the captive, and then execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng cited the Han precedent for a deposed rebel and asked that the emperor return to the capital, announce victory at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, present the captive, and only then execute him.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: This was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 中官王堂鎮浙江，請建生祠；

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Tang, commanding Zhejiang, asked to build a living shrine;
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Tang, who controlled Zhejiang, asked permission to build a living shrine to himself;

sentences.zh: 西番闡化王使者乞額外賜茶九萬斤。

translations.literal: envoys of the Western Barbarian King of Chánhua asked for an additional grant of ninety thousand jin of tea.
translations.idiomatic: and envoys of the King of Chánhua in the western borderlands asked for an extra ninety thousand jin of tea.

sentences.zh: 澄皆力爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Cheng strenuously opposed both; [the emperor] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng fought both proposals strenuously, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 王瓊欲陷彭澤，澄獨白其無罪。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong wished to frame Peng Ze; Cheng alone declared him innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong tried to frame Peng Ze, but Cheng alone testified to his innocence.

sentences.zh: 武宗崩，澄偕大學士梁儲、壽寧侯張鶴齡、駙馬崔元、太監韋霦等迎世宗於安陸。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died, Cheng joined Grand Secretary Liang Chu, Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling, Imperial Son-in-law Cui Yuan, the eunuch Wei Ying, and others in welcoming Shizong at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong died, Cheng joined Grand Secretary Liang Chu, Marquis of Shouning Zhang Heling, Imperial Son-in-law Cui Yuan, the eunuch Wei Ying, and others in going to Anlu to welcome the new emperor, Shizong.

sentences.zh: 既至，將謁見，有議用天子禮者。

translations.literal: When he arrived and was about to be received in audience, some proposed using the rites due to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived and was about to be received in audience, some argued that he should be greeted with the full rites reserved for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「今即如此，後何以加？

translations.literal: Cheng said: "If we do this now, what can be added later?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "If we treat him this way now, what ceremony will be left for his actual enthronement?

sentences.zh: 豈勸進、辭讓之禮當遂廢乎？」

translations.literal: Are the rites of urging acceptance and declining to be abandoned altogether?"
translations.idiomatic: Are we to abandon the rites of urging him to accept the throne and of his modest refusal?"

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼甫六日，有旨議興獻王主祀及尊稱。

translations.literal: Shizong had been on the throne only six days when an order came to deliberate the sacrificial duties toward Prince Xingxian and his honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Only six days after Shizong took the throne, an edict ordered deliberation on who should perform sacrifices to Prince Xingxian and what honorific title he should receive.

sentences.zh: 五月七日戊午，澄大會文武群臣，上議曰：「考漢成帝立定陶王為皇太子，立楚孝王孫景為定陶王，奉共王祀。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the fifth month, wuwu day, Cheng convened all civil and military officials and submitted a deliberation: "Considering how Emperor Cheng of Han made the Prince of Dingtao crown prince and installed Jing, grandson of the Prince of Chu Xiao, as Prince of Dingtao to perform sacrifices to Prince Gong.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the fifth month, a wuwu day, Cheng convened the full court and submitted a memorial: "When Emperor Cheng of Han made the Prince of Dingtao crown prince, he installed Jing, grandson of Prince Xiao of Chu, as the new Prince of Dingtao to maintain sacrifices to Prince Gong.

sentences.zh: 共王者，皇太子本生父也。

translations.literal: Prince Gong was the crown prince's biological father.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong was the crown prince's biological father.

sentences.zh: 時大司空師丹以為恩義備至。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan held that favor and duty had both been fully satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan held at the time that both favor and duty had been fully satisfied.

sentences.zh: 今陛下入承大統，宜如定陶王故事，以益王第二子崇仁王厚炫繼興王後，襲興王主祀事。

translations.literal: Now that Your Majesty has entered to inherit the great succession, you should follow the Dingtao precedent and have Houxuan, the Prince of Chongren and second son of the Prince of Yi, succeed as heir to the Prince of Xing and perform the sacrificial duties of the Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne, you should follow the Dingtao precedent: let Houxuan, the Prince of Chongren and second son of the Prince of Yi, succeed as heir to the Prince of Xing and perform sacrifices on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 又考宋濮安懿王之子入繼仁宗後，是為英宗。

translations.literal: Considering also how in Song the son of Prince Anyi of Pu entered to succeed Renzong and became Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: We also find the Song precedent: the son of Prince Anyi of Pu succeeded Emperor Renzong and became Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 司馬光謂濮王宜尊以高官大爵，稱王伯而不名。

translations.literal: Sima Guang said the Prince of Pu should be honored with high office and great rank, addressed as royal uncle without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang argued that the Prince of Pu should be honored with high office and great rank and addressed as royal uncle without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 範鎮亦言：『陛下既考仁宗，若復以濮王為考，於義未當。』

translations.literal: Fan Zhen also said: 'Since Your Majesty already takes Renzong as father, to take the Prince of Pu again as father would not be proper in ritual terms.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen also said, 'Since Your Majesty already regards Renzong as father, to regard the Prince of Pu as father as well would be ritually improper.

sentences.zh: 乃立濮王園廟，以宗樸為濮國公奉濮王祀。

translations.literal: A temple park was then established for the Prince of Pu, and Zongpu was made Duke of Pu to perform sacrifices to the Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: A temple park was established for the Prince of Pu, and Zongpu was made Duke of Pu to maintain his sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 程頤之言曰：『為人後者，謂所後為父母，而謂所生為伯、叔父母，此生人之大倫也。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi's words say: 'One who becomes another's heir calls the one he succeeds father and mother, and calls those who bore him uncle and aunt; this is the great human norm.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi wrote, 'An heir calls the person he succeeds father and mother, and calls his biological parents uncle and aunt; this is the fundamental human norm.

sentences.zh: 然所生之義，至尊至大，宜別立殊稱。

translations.literal: Yet the meaning of those who bore one is supremely exalted and great; a special title should be established separately.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bond with one's biological parents is supremely exalted; a special title should be established for them.

sentences.zh: 曰皇伯、叔父某國大王，則正統既明，而所生亦尊崇極矣。』

translations.literal: To call them Imperial Uncle, Royal Uncle, or Great King of such-and-such state would clarify the legitimate succession and also honor those who bore one to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Titles such as Imperial Uncle or Great King of a given state would clarify the legitimate succession while honoring one's biological parents to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 今興獻王於孝宗為弟，於陛下為本生父，與濮安懿王事正相等。

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Xingxian was younger brother to Xiaozong and is Your Majesty's biological father; the case is exactly parallel to that of Prince Anyi of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xingxian was Emperor Xiaozong's younger brother and is Your Majesty's biological father; the parallel with Prince Anyi of Pu is exact.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜稱孝宗為皇考，改稱興獻王為『皇叔父興獻大王』，妃為『皇叔母興獻王妃』。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should call Xiaozong Imperial Father and change the title of the Prince of Xingxian to 'Imperial Uncle, Great King of Xingxian' and his consort to 'Imperial Aunt, Consort of the King of Xingxian.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should call Emperor Xiaozong Imperial Father, and address the Prince of Xingxian as 'Imperial Uncle, Great King of Xingxian' and his consort as 'Imperial Aunt, Consort of the King of Xingxian.'

sentences.zh: 凡祭告興獻王及上箋於妃，俱自稱『侄皇帝』某，則正統、私親，恩禮兼盡，可以為萬世法。」

translations.literal: In all sacrifices announcing to the Prince of Xingxian and memorials to his consort, [Your Majesty] should style yourself 'Nephew Emperor' so-and-so; thus legitimate succession and private kinship, favor and ritual, would both be fully satisfied and could serve as law for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: In all communications to the prince and his consort, Your Majesty should style yourself 'Nephew Emperor' so-and-so; thus both legitimate succession and private kinship would be honored, and this could serve as a model for all time."

sentences.zh: 議上，帝怒曰：「父母可更易若是耶！」

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor angrily said: "Can one's parents be changed as easily as this!"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor angrily said, "Can one's parents be changed as easily as this!"

sentences.zh: 命再議。

translations.literal: He ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the court to deliberate again.

sentences.zh: 其月二十四日乙亥，澄復會廷臣上議曰：「《禮》為人後者為之子，自天子至庶人一也。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of that month, yihai day, Cheng again convened court officials and submitted a deliberation: "The Rites state that one who becomes another's heir becomes his son; this is the same from Son of Heaven down to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of that month, a yihai day, Cheng again convened the court and submitted a memorial: "The Rites teach that an heir becomes the son of the person he succeeds; this holds from the Son of Heaven down to the common people.

sentences.zh: 興獻王子惟陛下一人，既入繼大統，奉祀宗廟，是以臣等前議欲令崇仁王厚炫主興獻王祀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xingxian had only Your Majesty as son; having entered to inherit the great succession and perform sacrifices at the ancestral temple, we your subjects in our earlier deliberation wished to have the Prince of Chongren Houxuan perform sacrifices to the Prince of Xingxian.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xingxian had only Your Majesty as son; now that you have succeeded to the throne and sacrifice at the ancestral temple, we proposed earlier that the Prince of Chongren Houxuan should perform sacrifices to the Prince of Xingxian.

sentences.zh: 至於稱號，陛下宜稱為『皇叔父興獻大王』，自稱『侄皇帝』名。

translations.literal: As for titles, Your Majesty should address him as 'Imperial Uncle, Great King of Xingxian' and style yourself 'Nephew Emperor' with your personal name.
translations.idiomatic: As for titles, Your Majesty should address him as 'Imperial Uncle, Great King of Xingxian' and style yourself 'Nephew Emperor' followed by your personal name.

sentences.zh: 以宋程頤之說為可據也。

translations.literal: The words of Cheng Yi of Song may be taken as authority.
translations.idiomatic: This follows the authority of Cheng Yi of Song.

sentences.zh: 本朝之制，皇帝於宗藩尊行，止稱伯父、叔父，自稱皇帝而不名。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's regulation is that toward princes of the imperial clan in senior generation the emperor addresses them only as uncle or father's younger brother, and styles himself emperor without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Under our dynasty's regulations, the emperor addresses senior princes of the imperial clan only as uncle and styles himself emperor without using his personal name.

sentences.zh: 今稱興獻王為『皇叔父大王』，又自稱名，尊崇之典已至，臣等不敢復有所議。」

translations.literal: Now to call the Prince of Xingxian 'Imperial Uncle, Great King' and also use one's personal name—the ritual of honor has already reached its limit; we your subjects dare raise no further deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: To call the Prince of Xingxian 'Imperial Uncle, Great King' while using your personal name already exhausts the limits of honorific ritual; we dare raise no further objection."

sentences.zh: 因錄程頤《代彭思永議濮王禮疏》進覽。

translations.literal: They then transcribed Cheng Yi's "Memorial on the Rites of the Prince of Pu, Drafted for Peng Siyong" and submitted it for the emperor's perusal.
translations.idiomatic: They then submitted a copy of Cheng Yi's memorial on the rites of the Prince of Pu, drafted on behalf of Peng Siyong, for the emperor's review.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，命博考前代典禮，再議以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this and ordered a broad investigation of ritual precedents in former ages, with further deliberation to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered a thorough search of ritual precedents from earlier dynasties, with a further report to follow.

sentences.zh: 澄乃復會廷臣上議曰：「臣等會議者再，請改稱興獻王為叔父者，明大統之尊無二也。

translations.literal: Cheng then again convened court officials and submitted a deliberation: "We your subjects have met in deliberation twice; our request to change the title of the Prince of Xingxian to uncle was to make clear that the honor of the legitimate succession admits no second.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng convened the court again and submitted a memorial: "We have deliberated twice already. Our proposal to address the Prince of Xingxian as uncle was meant to show that the legitimate succession admits no rival.

sentences.zh: 然加『皇』字於『叔父』之上，則凡為陛下伯、叔諸父皆莫能與之齊矣。

translations.literal: Yet to add the character 'imperial' above 'uncle' means that none of all Your Majesty's uncles and father's younger brothers can be ranked equal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet adding the word 'imperial' before 'uncle' places him above every other uncle in the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 加『大』字於『王』之上，則天下諸王皆莫得而並之矣。

translations.literal: To add the character 'great' above 'king' means that none of all the princes under Heaven can be ranked equal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Adding the word 'great' before 'king' places him above every other prince in the realm.

sentences.zh: 興獻王稱號既定，則王妃稱號亦隨之，天下王妃亦無以同其尊矣。

translations.literal: Once the Prince of Xingxian's title is fixed, the consort's title follows it; no consort of a prince under Heaven can share his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Once the prince's title is fixed, his consort's title follows, and no other prince's consort can share that honor.

sentences.zh: 況陛下養以天下，所以樂其心，不違其誌，豈一家一國之養可同日語哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty supports him with all under Heaven to delight his heart and not go against his wishes—how can the support of one family or one state be spoken of in the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty sustains him with the resources of the entire realm to delight his heart and honor his wishes; how can the support of a single household or fief be mentioned in the same breath?

sentences.zh: 此孔子所謂事之以禮者。

translations.literal: This is what Confucius called serving them with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Confucius meant by serving one's parents with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 其他推尊之說，稱親之議，似為非禮。

translations.literal: Other proposals to exalt him further and to call him father seem to be contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Other proposals to exalt him further or to call him father seem contrary to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 推尊之非，莫詳於魏明帝之詔。

translations.literal: The error of excessive exaltation is nowhere set forth more fully than in the edict of Emperor Ming of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The error of excessive exaltation is nowhere explained more fully than in the edict of Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 稱親之非，莫詳於宋程頤之議。

translations.literal: The error of calling him father is nowhere set forth more fully than in the deliberation of Cheng Yi of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The error of calling him father is nowhere explained more fully than in the deliberation of Cheng Yi of Song.

sentences.zh: 至當之禮，要不出於此。」

translations.literal: The most fitting rites must lie within this."
translations.idiomatic: The most fitting ritual conduct cannot lie outside these principles."

sentences.zh: 並錄上魏明帝詔書。

translations.literal: He also appended and submitted the edict of Emperor Ming of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He also appended and submitted the edict of Emperor Ming of Wei.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝銳意欲推崇所生，而進士張璁復抗疏極言禮官之謬。

translations.literal: At that time, the Emperor keenly wished to exalt his biological father, while the presented scholar Zhang Cong again submitted a bold memorial vehemently stating the errors of the ritual officials.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was keen to exalt his biological father, and the presented scholar Zhang Cong again submitted a forceful memorial denouncing the ritual officials' errors.

sentences.zh: 帝心動，持澄等疏久不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was moved; he kept Mao Cheng and others' memorial for a long time without issuing a decision.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was swayed and held Mao Cheng's memorial and the others' without acting on it for some time.

sentences.zh: 至八月庚辰朔，再命集議。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, the cyclical day gengchen, he again ordered a collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month (the day gengchen), he ordered deliberation convened again.

sentences.zh: 澄等乃復上議曰：「先王制禮，本乎人情。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng and others then again submitted a deliberation, saying: "The former kings instituted rites based upon human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng and his colleagues submitted another memorial, saying: "Former kings fashioned ritual based on human feeling.

sentences.zh: 武宗既無子嗣，又鮮兄弟，援立陛下於憲廟諸孫之中。

translations.literal: Wuzong had neither heirs nor, scarcely, brothers; he drew forth and established Your Majesty among the grandsons of the Xianzong temple line.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wuzong had no son and almost no brothers, he raised Your Majesty from among the grandsons of the Xianzong lineage.

sentences.zh: 是武宗以陛下為同堂之弟，考孝宗，母慈壽，無可疑矣，可復顧私親哉？」

translations.literal: Thus Wuzong took Your Majesty as a same-hall younger brother; to take Xiaozong as father and Cishou as mother admits no doubt—how could one again attend to private kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wuzong treated Your Majesty as a younger brother of the same generation; to regard Xiaozong as father and Empress Dowager Cishou as mother is beyond dispute—how then turn again to private kinship?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝不懌，復留中。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor was displeased and again retained it in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When it reached the throne, the emperor was displeased and again kept it at court without acting.

sentences.zh: 會給事中邢寰請議憲廟皇妃邵氏徽號，澄上言：「王妃誕生獻王，實陛下所自出。

translations.literal: It happened that the supervising secretary Xing Huan requested deliberation on the honorific title of the Xianzong-temple imperial consort Lady Shao; Mao Cheng submitted, saying: "The princess consort gave birth to the Prince of Xing—she is in truth the source from which Your Majesty issued.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the supervising secretary Xing Huan asked that the honorific title of Lady Shao, imperial consort of the Xianzong temple, be debated; Mao Cheng wrote: "The princess consort bore the Prince of Xing—she is truly Your Majesty's birth mother.

sentences.zh: 但既承大統，則宜考孝宗，而母慈壽太后矣。

translations.literal: But having already succeeded to the great succession, one should take Xiaozong as father and regard Cishou as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having assumed the great succession, Your Majesty should take Xiaozong as father and regard Empress Dowager Cishou as mother.

sentences.zh: 孝宗於憲廟皇妃宜稱皇太妃，則在陛下宜稱太皇太妃。

translations.literal: Toward Xiaozong the Xianzong-temple imperial consort should be called Grand Imperial Consort; toward Your Majesty she should be called Grand Empress Dowager Consort.
translations.idiomatic: As between Xiaozong and the Xianzong imperial consort she should be titled Grand Imperial Consort; for Your Majesty she should be titled Grand Empress Dowager Consort.

sentences.zh: 如此，則彜倫既正，恩義亦篤。」

translations.literal: In this way, human relations would be set right and grace and righteousness would also be deep."
translations.idiomatic: In this way human order would be corrected and both grace and duty would be secured."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and noted.

sentences.zh: 其月，帝以母妃將至，下禮官議其儀。

translations.literal: That month, as the imperial mother consort was about to arrive, the Emperor sent down [orders] to the ritual officials to deliberate on the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: That month, with his birth mother soon to arrive, the emperor directed the ritual officials to deliberate the ceremonial protocol.

sentences.zh: 澄等請由崇文門入東安門，帝不可。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng and others requested entry by the Chongwen Gate and the Dong'an Gate; the Emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng and others proposed entry through Chongwen Gate and Dong'an Gate; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃議由正陽左門入大明東門，帝又不可。

translations.literal: They then deliberated entry by the Zhengyang Left Gate and the Great Ming Eastern Gate; the Emperor again would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: They then proposed the Zhengyang Left Gate and the Great Ming Eastern Gate; the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 澄等執議如初。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng and others held to their original deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng and the others held to their original proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝乃自定其儀，悉由中門入。

translations.literal: The Emperor then fixed the ceremony himself: all would enter by the central gates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then set the ceremony himself, ordering entry entirely through the central gates.

sentences.zh: 時尊崇禮猶未定，張璁復進《大禮或問》，帝益向之。

translations.literal: At the time the rites of exaltation and respect were still unsettled; Zhang Cong again presented "Questions on the Great Rites," and the Emperor leaned toward him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: As rites for honoring his parents were still undecided, Zhang Cong again submitted Questions on the Great Rites, and the emperor inclined toward him all the more.

sentences.zh: 至九月末，乃下澄等前疏，更令博采輿論以聞。

translations.literal: At the end of the ninth month he finally issued Mao Cheng and others' earlier memorial, and again ordered broad gathering of public opinion to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the ninth month he finally released Mao Cheng's earlier memorial and ordered a wider canvass of opinion to be reported.

sentences.zh: 澄等知勢不可已，謀於內閣，加稱興王為『帝』，妃為「後」，而以皇太后懿旨行之。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng and others knew the momentum could not be stopped; they schemed with the Grand Secretariat to add the title "Emperor" to the Prince of Xing and "Empress" to the consort, and to carry it out by the empress dowager's gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing the tide could not be turned, Mao Cheng and his colleagues consulted the Grand Secretariat: add "Emperor" to the Prince of Xing and "Empress" to his consort, and implement it under the empress dowager's edict.

sentences.zh: 乃疏言：「臣等一得之愚，已盡於前議。

translations.literal: They then memorialized, saying: "Your servants' trifling one-time understanding has been exhausted in the previous deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized: "Your servants have set forth our modest views fully in the prior deliberation.

sentences.zh: 茲欲仰慰聖心，使宜於今而不戾乎情，合乎古而無悖乎義，則有密勿股肱在。

translations.literal: Now wishing to look up and soothe the sagely heart—so that what suits the present does not run contrary to feeling, and what accords with antiquity does not violate righteousness—the intimate, assiduous limbs-and-trunk are at hand.
translations.idiomatic: To comfort the imperial mind now—to suit the present without violating feeling, and fit antiquity without breaching duty—there are your intimate counselors at hand.

sentences.zh: 臣等有司，未敢擅任。」

translations.literal: Your servant-officials as responsible departments dare not presume to undertake it on their own."
translations.idiomatic: We your subordinate officials dare not assume that responsibility unilaterally."

sentences.zh: 帝遂於十月二日庚辰，以慈壽皇太后旨加興獻王號曰「興獻帝」，妃曰「興國太后」，皇妃邵氏亦尊為「皇太后」，宣示中外。

translations.literal: The Emperor then, on the second day of the tenth month, cyclical day gengchen, by the edict of Empress Dowager Cishou added to the Prince of Xingxian the title "Emperor Xingxian," to the consort "Empress of Xing," and also exalted Imperial Consort Shao as "Empress Dowager," proclaiming it within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the tenth month (the day gengchen), by edict of Empress Dowager Cishou the emperor added the title Emperor Xingxian to the Prince of Xingxian, titled his consort Empress of Xing, also honored Imperial Consort Shao as Empress Dowager, and proclaimed this at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 顧帝雖勉從廷議，意猶慊之。

translations.literal: Yet though the Emperor reluctantly followed court deliberation, in his mind he was still unsatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had reluctantly followed court deliberation, the emperor remained dissatisfied at heart.

sentences.zh: 十二月十一日己丑，復傳諭加稱皇帝。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month, cyclical day jichou, he again transmitted an order to add the title Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month (the day jichou) he again issued orders to add the title Emperor.

sentences.zh: 內閣楊廷和等封還禦批，澄抗疏力爭，又偕九卿喬宇等合諫，帝皆不允。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat—Yang Tinghe and others—sealed and returned the imperial rescript; Mao Cheng submitted a bold memorial struggling forcefully; he also joined the Nine Ministers Qiao Yu and others in a joint remonstrance; the Emperor denied all.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe and the Grand Secretariat returned the imperial rescript sealed; Mao Cheng submitted a forceful memorial of protest; he joined the Nine Ministers led by Qiao Yu in joint remonstrance—the emperor denied them all.

sentences.zh: 明年，嘉靖改元正月，清寧宮後三小宮災。

translations.literal: The next year, in the first month when the reign title was changed to Jiajing, the three small palaces behind Qingning Palace were consumed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the first month of the new Jiajing reign, fire destroyed the three small palaces behind Qingning Palace.

sentences.zh: 澄復以為言，會朝臣亦多諫者，事獲止。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng again spoke on it; it happened that many court officials also remonstrated, and the matter was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng raised the matter again; many court officials also remonstrated, and the plan was stopped.

sentences.zh: 澄端亮有學行，論事侃侃不撓。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng was upright and bright, possessed learning and conduct; in discussing affairs he spoke forthrightly and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng was upright and learned; in debate he spoke plainly and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 帝欲推尊所生，嘗遣中官諭意，至長跪稽首。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to exalt his biological father; he once sent a palace eunuch to convey his intent, even to the point of kneeling long and bowing to the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to honor his biological father, he once sent a palace eunuch to convey his wishes, who went so far as to kneel and perform full prostrations.

sentences.zh: 澄駭愕，急扶之起。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng was startled and astonished; he hurriedly helped him up.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng was alarmed and hastily helped him rise.

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「上意也。

translations.literal: The man said: "This is the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The man said: "This is His Majesty's meaning.

sentences.zh: 上言『人孰無父母，奈何使我不獲伸』，必祈公易議。」

translations.literal: The sovereign says, 'Who lacks parents—why should you keep me from giving full expression?'—he must beg you, sir, to alter the deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Who is without parents—why will you not let me give full expression?' He urges you to change your position in deliberation."

sentences.zh: 因出囊金畀澄。

translations.literal: He then produced gold from his pouch and gave it to Mao Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then took gold from his purse and offered it to Mao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄奮然曰：「老臣悖耄，不能隳典禮。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng said with vehemence: "This old official is perverse and senile; he cannot destroy canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng said hotly: "This old official is dull and senile; I cannot wreck the canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 獨有一去，不與議已耳。」

translations.literal: There is only leaving office—not joining the deliberation, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I can only withdraw and decline to join the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 抗疏引疾至五六上，帝輒慰留不允。

translations.literal: He submitted bold memorials citing illness, up to five or six times; the Emperor always comforted him and detained him, not granting leave.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted repeated memorials citing illness, five or six times; each time the emperor comforted him and refused leave.

sentences.zh: 二年二月疾甚，復力請，乃許之。

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, his illness was severe; he again pressed his request forcefully, and leave was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign, by the second month his illness was severe; he pressed his request again and was granted leave.

sentences.zh: 舟至興濟而卒。

translations.literal: When his boat reached Xingji, he died.
translations.idiomatic: His boat reached Xingji, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 先是，論定策功，加澄太子太傅，蔭錦衣世指揮同知，力辭不受。

translations.literal: Earlier, when deliberating rewards for fixing the succession, Mao Cheng was advanced to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; hereditary enfeoffment as Vice Commissioner of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard was bestowed—he pressed to decline and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when settling rewards for establishing the succession, he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted hereditary enfeoffment as Vice Commissioner in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he firmly declined both.

sentences.zh: 帝雅敬憚澄，雖數忤旨，而恩禮不衰。

translations.literal: The Emperor always respected and feared Mao Cheng; though he repeatedly opposed the imperial intent, favor and ritual courtesies did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always respected and feared him; though he repeatedly opposed imperial wishes, imperial favor and ceremonial regard never waned.

sentences.zh: 既得疾，遣醫診視，藥物之賜時至。

translations.literal: Once he fell ill, physicians were sent to examine him; gifts of medicines arrived from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Once he fell ill, the emperor sent physicians and medicines arrived again and again.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，深悼惜之。

translations.literal: At his death, the Emperor deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈少傅，謚文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Junior Grand Preceptor and the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenjian ("Cultured and Simple").

sentences.zh: 汪俊，字抑之，弋陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, style Yizhi, a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, whose style name was Yizhi, was a native of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 父鳳，進士，貴州參政。

translations.literal: His father Feng was a presented scholar and Guizhou Administration Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Feng was a presented scholar and Vice Commissioner of the Guizhou Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 俊舉弘治六年會試第一，授庶吉士，進編修。

translations.literal: Jun placed first in the metropolitan examination of the sixth year of Hongzhi; he was appointed Academic Expositor, and advanced to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun ranked first in the metropolitan examination of Hongzhi 6; he was made a Hanlin bachelor and later promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 正德中，與修《孝宗實錄》，以不附劉瑾、焦芳，調南京工部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period, while collaborating on the Veritable Records of Xiaozong, because he did not adhere to Liu Jin and Jiao Fang, he was transferred to Nanjing Ministry of Works—Outside Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengde, while compiling the Veritable Records of Xiaozong, he refused to side with Liu Jin and Jiao Fang and was transferred to Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 瑾、芳敗，召復原官。

translations.literal: When Jin and Fang fell, he was summoned back to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin and Fang fell, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader-in-Waiting Bachelor, then elevated to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments to Reader-in-Waiting and then to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年轉吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時議興獻王尊號，與尚書喬宇、毛澄輩力爭。

translations.literal: At the time when the honorific title of the Prince of Xingxian was deliberated, he struggled forcefully with Ministers Qiao Yu, Mao Cheng, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When the title for the Prince of Xingxian was debated, he fought alongside Ministers Qiao Yu and Mao Cheng and their allies.

sentences.zh: 澄引疾去，代者羅欽順不至，乃以俊為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng cited illness and left; the replacement Luo Qinshun did not arrive; Wang Jun was then made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Cheng retired citing illness, his intended successor Luo Qinshun failed to take up the post, and Wang Jun was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 是時獻王已加帝號矣，主事桂萼復請稱皇考。

translations.literal: By then the Prince of Xing had already been given the title Emperor; the department director Gui E again requested that he be called Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Prince of Xing had already been given an imperial title; Department Director Gui E again asked that he be titled Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 章下廷議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，俊集廷臣七十有三人上議曰：「祖訓『兄終弟及』，指同產言。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Wang Jun gathered seventy-three court ministers and submitted a deliberation, saying: "The ancestral instruction 'when the elder brother ends, the younger brother succeeds' refers to full uterine brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year three, Wang Jun gathered seventy-three court officials and submitted a deliberation: "The ancestral teaching 'when the elder brother dies, the younger brother succeeds' refers to full brothers of one mother.

sentences.zh: 今陛下為武宗親弟，自宜考孝宗明矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is Wuzong's uterine younger brother; that one should take Xiaozong as father is clear indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Wuzong's full younger brother; that you should regard Xiaozong as father is plainly established.

sentences.zh: 孰謂與人為後，而滅武宗之統也。

translations.literal: Who would say that becoming another's heir extinguishes Wuzong's line?
translations.idiomatic: Who says that becoming another's heir extinguishes Wuzong's succession?

sentences.zh: 《儀禮》傳曰：『為人後者，孰後？

translations.literal: The commentary on the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial says: "One who becomes another's heir—whose heir?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou commentary asks: "He who becomes another's heir—whose heir is he?

sentences.zh: 後大宗也。』

translations.literal: The heir to the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The heir to the great lineage.

sentences.zh: 漢宣起民間，猶嗣孝昭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han rose from among the people yet still succeeded Xiaozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han rose from common life yet still succeeded Emperor Zhao.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，猶考孝元。

translations.literal: Guangwu in restoring the dynasty still took Xiaoyuan as father in worship.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu in restoring the house still took Emperor Yuan as his ancestral father.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝詔皇后無子，擇建支子，以繼大宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei's edict: when the empress had no son, choose and establish a branch son to continue the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei decreed: when the empress had no son, select and establish a branch son to continue the great lineage.

sentences.zh: 孰謂入繼之主與為人後者異也。

translations.literal: Who would say that a lord who enters succession differs from one who becomes another's heir?
translations.idiomatic: Who says a ruler who enters by succession differs from one who becomes another's heir?

sentences.zh: 宋範純仁謂英宗親受詔為子，與入繼不同，蓋言恩義尤篤，尤當不顧私親，非以生前為子者乃為人後，身後入繼者不為人後也。

translations.literal: Fan Chunren of Song said that Yingzong personally received the edict to become a son, differing from entering succession—this broadly speaks of grace and righteousness being especially deep, and that one should especially not attend to private kin; it is not that one who became a son in life is becoming another's heir while one who enters succession after death is not becoming another's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunren of Song said that Yingzong personally received the edict to become a son, unlike mere entry by succession—meaning that when grace and duty are especially binding, private kin must be set aside all the more; he did not mean that only one adopted in life is "becoming another's heir" while one who enters succession after death is not.

sentences.zh: 萼言『孝宗既有武宗為之子，安得復為立後。』

translations.literal: Gui E said, "Xiaozong already has Wuzong as son—how could one again establish an heir for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E said, "Xiaozong already has Wuzong as his son—how can one establish another heir for him?

sentences.zh: 臣等謂陛下自後武宗而上考孝宗，非為孝宗立後也。

translations.literal: Your servants say that Your Majesty, from succeeding Wuzong upward, takes Xiaozong as father in worship—not that one is establishing an heir for Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that in succeeding Wuzong and taking Xiaozong as father, Your Majesty is not establishing an heir for Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 又言『武宗全神器授陛下，何忍不繼其統。』

translations.literal: He also said, "Wuzong entrusted the entire regalia to Your Majesty—how could one bear not to continue his line?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Wuzong entrusted the entire regalia to Your Majesty—how can you bear not to continue his line?

sentences.zh: 臣等謂陛下既稱武宗皇兄矣，豈必改孝宗稱伯，乃為繼其統乎？

translations.literal: Your servants say that since Your Majesty already calls Wuzong imperial elder brother, must one change Xiaozong to "uncle" before one is continuing his line?
translations.idiomatic: We say that since Your Majesty already calls Wuzong imperial elder brother, must you change Xiaozong to "uncle" before you are continuing Wuzong's line?

sentences.zh: 又言『禮官執者不過前宋《濮議》』。

translations.literal: He also said, "What the ritual officials hold to is nothing beyond the former Song 'Deliberation on Pu'.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The ritual officials' position is nothing but the Song Pu Deliberation."

sentences.zh: 臣等愚昧，所執實不出此。

translations.literal: Your servants are dull and ignorant; what we hold to in truth does not depart from this.
translations.idiomatic: We are dull, but what we uphold does not depart from this.

sentences.zh: 蓋宋程頤之議曰：『雖當專意於正統，豈得盡絕於私恩。

translations.literal: For Cheng Yi of Song's deliberation says: "Though one must focus intent on the orthodox succession, how could one utterly cut off private grace?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi of Song argued: "Though one must focus on the orthodox line, one cannot utterly sever private affection.

sentences.zh: 故所繼，主於大義；

translations.literal: Therefore the one succeeded to is governed by great principle;
translations.idiomatic: The succession upheld serves great principle;

sentences.zh: 所生，存乎至情。

translations.literal: the one who gave birth is preserved in utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: the one who gave birth is preserved in utmost feeling.

sentences.zh: 至於名稱，統緒所系，若其無別，斯亂大倫。』

translations.literal: As for names and titles, upon which lineage coherence depends—if there is no distinction, that disorders the great human relations.
translations.idiomatic: As for titles, on which lineage coherence depends—if there is no distinction, the great human order is thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 殆為今日發也。

translations.literal: It was nearly spoken for today.
translations.idiomatic: These words might have been spoken for our own day.

sentences.zh: 謹集諸章奏，惟進士張璁、主事霍韜、給事中熊浹與萼議同，其他八十余疏二百五十余人，皆如臣等議。」

translations.literal: We respectfully gathered all memorials: only the presented scholar Zhang Cong, the department director Huo Tao, the supervising secretary Xiong Jian, and Gui E share the same deliberation; the other eighty-plus memorials from more than two hundred fifty persons all agree with your servants' deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: We have gathered all memorials: only presented scholar Zhang Cong, department director Huo Tao, supervising secretary Xiong Jian, and Gui E share Gui E's view; the other eighty-plus memorials from more than two hundred fifty officials all agree with our position."

sentences.zh: 議上，留中。

translations.literal: When the deliberation went up, it was retained in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was submitted and held at court.

sentences.zh: 而特旨召桂萼、張璁、席書於南京。

translations.literal: Yet by special edict Gui E, Zhang Cong, and Xi Shu were summoned from Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict, Gui E, Zhang Cong, and Xi Shu were summoned from Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 越旬有五日，乃下諭曰：「朕奉承宗廟正統，大義豈敢有違。

translations.literal: After ten and five days had passed, an order was issued, saying: "We receive and uphold the orthodox succession of the ancestral temples—how would we dare violate the great principle?
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen days later an edict was issued: "We uphold the orthodox succession of the ancestral temples—how dare we violate the great principle?

sentences.zh: 第本生至情，亦當兼盡。

translations.literal: Only the utmost feeling toward the biological parent must also be fully met.
translations.idiomatic: Yet feeling toward our biological parent must also be fully honored.

sentences.zh: 其再集議以聞。」

translations.literal: Deliberate again and report."
translations.idiomatic: Convene deliberation again and report.

sentences.zh: 俊不得已，乃集群臣請加「皇」字，以全徽稱。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, having no alternative, then gathered the ministers and requested adding the character "Imperial" to complete the honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, with no choice, gathered the ministers and asked that the character "Imperial" be added to complete the honorific.

sentences.zh: 議上，復留十余日。

translations.literal: When the deliberation went up, it was again retained for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was submitted and again held for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 至三月朔，乃詔禮官，加稱興獻帝為本「生皇考恭穆獻皇帝」，興國太后為「本生母章聖皇太后」。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, he then ordered the ritual officials: add to Emperor Xingxian the title "Biological Imperial Father, Respectful and Solemn, Emperor Xian"; to the Empress of Xing, "Biological Mother, Zhangsheng, Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month he ordered the ritual officials: add for Emperor Xingxian the title "Biological Imperial Father, Respectful and Solemn Emperor Xian," and for the Empress of Xing "Biological Mother, Zhangsheng, Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: 擇日祭告郊廟，頒詔天下。

translations.literal: A day was chosen to offer sacrifice and report to the suburban altars and ancestral temples; an edict was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A date was chosen to report to the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and an edict was promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 而別諭建室奉先殿側，恭祀獻皇。

translations.literal: Separately he ordered a chamber built beside the Hall for Venerating Ancestors to honor the Xian emperor with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered a separate chamber built beside the Hall for Venerating Ancestors to honor the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 俊等復爭曰：「陛下入奉大宗，不得祭小宗，亦猶小宗之不得祭大宗也。

translations.literal: Wang Jun and others again struggled, saying: "Your Majesty, in entering to serve the great lineage, may not sacrifice to the lesser lineage—just as the lesser lineage may not sacrifice to the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun and others protested again: "Your Majesty, having entered to serve the great lineage, cannot sacrifice to the lesser lineage—just as the lesser lineage cannot sacrifice to the great.

sentences.zh: 昔興獻帝奉藩安陸，則不得祭憲宗。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Xingxian, holding fief at Anlu, could not sacrifice to Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Prince of Xing, holding his fief at Anlu, could not sacrifice to Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 今陛下入繼大統，亦不得祭興獻帝。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, entering to succeed to the great succession, likewise may not sacrifice to Emperor Xingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has entered the great succession, you likewise cannot sacrifice to the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 是皆以禮抑情者也。

translations.literal: In all cases ritual restrains feeling.
translations.idiomatic: In each case ritual restrains personal feeling.

sentences.zh: 然興獻帝不得迎養壽安皇太后於藩邸，陛下得迎興國太后於大內，受天下之養，而尊祀興獻帝以天子之禮樂，則人子之情獲自盡矣。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Xingxian could not receive and support the Shou'an empress dowager at his fief residence; Your Majesty can receive the Empress of Xing into the inner palace, receive the nourishment of the realm, and honor Emperor Xingxian with the rites and music of the Son of Heaven—then the feeling of a human child may find its own fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Xing could not receive Empress Dowager Shou'an at his fief; Your Majesty can receive the Empress of Xing into the inner palace, receive the empire's support, and honor the Prince of Xing with a Son of Heaven's rites and music—thus a son's feeling may be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 乃今聖心無窮，臣等敢不將順，但於正統無嫌，乃為合禮。」

translations.literal: Now if the sagely heart is boundless, your servants would not dare fail to comply and accord—but only what raises no doubt toward the orthodox succession is ritually fitting."
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial mind is boundless, we dare not fail to comply—but only what does not compromise the orthodox succession is ritually proper.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕但欲奉先殿側別建一室，以伸追慕之情耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "We only wish to build a separate chamber beside the Hall for Venerating Ancestors to extend the feeling of remembrance and longing—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "We only wish to build a separate chamber beside the Hall for Venerating Ancestors to express our longing—that is all.

sentences.zh: 迎養藩邸，祖宗朝無此例，何容飾以為詞。

translations.literal: Receiving and supporting at a fief residence—in the reigns of our forefathers there was no such precedent; how could one embellish it as an argument?
translations.idiomatic: Receiving and supporting at a princely residence—no such precedent exists in our ancestral reigns; how can you dress that up as an argument?

sentences.zh: 其令陳狀。」

translations.literal: Order them to set forth their reasons in writing."
translations.idiomatic: Have them submit written explanations.

sentences.zh: 俊具疏引罪。

translations.literal: Wang Jun submitted a full memorial acknowledging guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun submitted a full memorial acknowledging fault.

sentences.zh: 用嚴旨切責，而趣立廟益急。

translations.literal: Thereupon stern edicts were used to rebuke sharply, while urging temple construction grew all the more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued stern rebukes by edict and pressed ever harder to have the temple built.

sentences.zh: 俊等乃上議曰：「立廟大內，有幹正統。

translations.literal: Jun and others then submitted a deliberation, saying: "To establish a temple within the Inner Palace would impinge upon the orthodox succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun and his colleagues then submitted a memorial: "Building a temple inside the Inner Palace would compromise the orthodox succession.

sentences.zh: 臣實愚昧，不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Your servants are truly ignorant and do not dare obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: We are truly obtuse and dare not obey this order.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，而令集廷臣大議。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept it, but ordered the court ministers gathered for a great deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected their view and ordered a full court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 俊等復上議曰：「謹按先朝奉慈別殿，蓋孝宗皇帝為孝穆皇太后附葬初畢，神主無薦享之所而設也。

translations.literal: Jun and others again submitted a deliberation, saying: "We respectfully note that in the previous reign the separate Fengci Hall was established because, when Emperor Xiaozong's burial of Empress Xiaomu had just been completed, there was no place for offering and sacrifice to her spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted again: "We respectfully observe that the separate Fengci Hall of the previous reign was created because, when Emperor Xiaozong had just completed the joint burial of Empress Xiaomu, there was nowhere to offer sacrifices to her spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 當時議者，皆據周制特祀姜原而言。

translations.literal: The deliberators of that time all spoke on the basis of the Zhou institution of special sacrifice to Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters of that day all cited the Zhou practice of specially honoring Jiang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 至為本生立廟大內，則從古未聞。

translations.literal: As for establishing a temple within the Inner Palace for one's birth parent, from antiquity it has never been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: But to establish a temple in the Inner Palace for one's birth father—never has such a thing been heard in all antiquity.

sentences.zh: 惟漢哀帝為定陶恭王立廟京師。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Ai of Han built a temple in the capital for Prince Gong of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: The sole precedent is Emperor Ai of Han, who built a temple in the capital for Prince Gong of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 師丹以為不可，哀帝不聽，卒遺後世之譏。

translations.literal: Shi Dan held it impermissible; Emperor Ai did not heed him, and in the end left ridicule to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dan declared it unacceptable; Emperor Ai refused to listen and ended up a laughingstock to posterity.

sentences.zh: 陛下有可以為堯、舜之資，臣等不敢導以衰世之事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty possesses the endowment to be a Yao or Shun; your servants dare not guide you with affairs of a declining age.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has the capacity to rival Yao and Shun; we dare not steer you toward the errors of a decadent age.

sentences.zh: 請於安陸特建獻帝百世不遷之廟，俟他日襲封興王子孫世世獻饗，陛下歲時遣官持節奉祀，亦足伸陛下無窮至情矣。」

translations.literal: We ask that at Anlu a temple be specially built for the Xian emperor, not to be moved for a hundred generations; when in future days the descendants of the Prince of Xing who succeed to the fief offer sacrifice generation after generation, Your Majesty may each year dispatch officials bearing credentials to perform the rites—this too would suffice to extend Your Majesty's boundless utmost feeling."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that a perpetual temple for the Prince of Xing be built at Anlu, where his enfeoffed descendants may offer sacrifice for generations, while Your Majesty sends credentialed officials annually to perform the rites—enough, surely, to satisfy your boundless devotion.

sentences.zh: 帝仍命遵前旨再議，俊遂抗疏乞休。

translations.literal: The Emperor still ordered obedience to the previous instruction and further deliberation; Jun thereupon submitted a defiant memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still insisted they follow his earlier order and deliberate again; Wang Jun then submitted a bold memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 再請益力，帝怒，責以肆慢，允其去。

translations.literal: When he petitioned again still more forcefully, the Emperor grew angry, rebuked him for insolent disrespect, and granted his departure.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed his request with greater force, the emperor flew into a rage, accused him of brazen disrespect, and allowed him to leave office.

sentences.zh: 召席書未至，令吳一鵬署事。

translations.literal: Xi Shu was summoned but had not yet arrived; Wu Yipeng was ordered to assume affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu was summoned but had not yet arrived, so Wu Yipeng was put in charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 《明倫大典》成，落俊職，卒於家。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Canon of Human Relations was completed, Jun was removed from office; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Canon of Human Relations was completed, Wang Jun was dismissed from his post and died at home.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈少保，謚文莊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian; his posthumous title was Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was posthumously made Junior Guardian with the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 俊行誼修潔，立朝光明端介。

translations.literal: Jun's conduct and friendship were cultivated and pure; in court he was bright, upright, and sharp-edged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's conduct was refined and immaculate; in office he was forthright and incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 學宗洛、閩。

translations.literal: In learning he took the Luo and Fujian schools as masters.
translations.idiomatic: His learning followed the Luo River and Fujian traditions.

sentences.zh: 與王守仁交好，而不同其說。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Wang Shouren but did not agree with his doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Wang Yangming but rejected his teachings.

sentences.zh: 學者稱「石潭先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars called him "Master Shitan."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars called him Master Shitan.

sentences.zh: 弟偉，字器之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wei, style Qizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei, styled Qizhi.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授檢討。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Hanlin bachelor to the post of reviser.

sentences.zh: 與俊皆忤劉瑾，調南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: Both he and Jun offended Liu Jin and were transferred to Principal Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Jun both crossed Liu Jin and were transferred to Nanjing as principal secretaries in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復故官。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, they were restored to their former offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution they recovered their former posts.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became Rector of the Nanjing National University.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to become Rector of the Nanjing National University.

sentences.zh: 武宗以巡幸至，率諸生請幸學，不從。

translations.literal: When Wuzong arrived on a tour of inspection, he led the students in requesting that the emperor visit the academy; the emperor did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came on an inspection tour, Wei led the students in pleading that the emperor visit the academy, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 江彬矯旨取玉硯，偉曰：「有秀才時故硯，可持去。」

translations.literal: Jiang Bin forged an edict to seize a jade inkstone; Wei said: "There is the old inkstone from when one was a xiucai—you may take that."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin forged an edict to seize a jade inkstone; Wei said: "Take the old inkstone I used as a licentiate, if you like.

sentences.zh: 俊罷官之歲，偉亦至吏部右侍郎，偕廷臣數爭「大禮」，又伏闕力爭。

translations.literal: In the year Jun left office, Wei also reached Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Personnel; with court ministers he repeatedly disputed the "Great Rites," and again prostrated himself at the palace gate to struggle forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The year Wang Jun left office, Wei had risen to Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Personnel; he joined court ministers in repeated disputes over the Great Rites and once more threw himself before the palace gate in fierce protest.

sentences.zh: 及席書、張璁等議行，猶持前說不變。

translations.literal: When Xi Shu, Zhang Cong, and others' deliberations were implemented, he still held to his former view without change.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the policies of Xi Shu and Zhang Cong took effect, he clung to his original position.

sentences.zh: 轉官左侍郎，為陳氵光劾罷，卒於家。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Minister of the left, he was impeached and dismissed by Chen Guang; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of the left, he was impeached and removed by Chen Guang and died at home.

sentences.zh: 吳一鵬，字南夫，長洲人。

translations.literal: Wu Yipeng, style Nanfu, a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yipeng, whose style name was Nanfu, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of Hongzhi 6.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 遷庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor and then appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書周經以讒去，上疏乞留之。

translations.literal: When Minister of Revenue Zhou Jing left office on account of slander, he submitted a memorial begging that Jing be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Zhou Jing was driven out by slander, Wu submitted a memorial asking that he be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 正德初，進侍講，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was advanced to Court Lecturer and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was promoted to Court Lecturer and served on the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾出諸翰林為部曹，一鵬得南京刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Liu Jin sent out the Hanlin academicians to departmental posts; Yipeng received the post of Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin expelled the Hanlin academicians to ministry posts; Wu Yipeng was made Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復為侍講。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was restored as Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was restored as Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 進侍講學士，歷國子祭酒、太常卿。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Lecturing Academician and successively held the posts of Rector of the National University and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Lecturing Academician and served successively as Rector of the National University and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 並在南京。

translations.literal: All these posts were in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: All of these posts were in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 母喪除，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，召拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor took the throne, Wu was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋轉左。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 數與尚書毛澄、汪俊力爭「大禮」。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he struggled forcefully with Ministers Mao Cheng and Wang Jun over the "Great Rites."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly fought the Great Rites policy alongside Ministers Mao Cheng and Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊去國，一鵬署部事，而帝趣建獻帝廟甚亟。

translations.literal: When Jun left the state, Yipeng assumed ministry affairs, while the Emperor urged construction of the Xian emperor's temple with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jun left office, Wu Yipeng took charge of the ministry while the emperor pressed urgently to build a temple to the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 一鵬集廷臣上議曰：「前世入繼之君，間有為本生立廟園陵及京師者。

translations.literal: Yipeng gathered the court ministers and submitted a deliberation, saying: "Among former emperors who entered by succession, there have occasionally been cases of building temples at the garden tomb or in the capital for the birth parent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yipeng gathered the court and submitted a memorial: "Among earlier emperors who succeeded by adoption, some did build temples at their birth parents' tombs or in the capital.

sentences.zh: 第歲時遣官致祀，尋亦奏罷。

translations.literal: But they only dispatched officials at the seasons to perform sacrifice, and soon memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they sent officials only for seasonal sacrifices and soon petitioned to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 然猶見非當時，取議後代。

translations.literal: Yet they were still condemned in their own day and became subjects of debate for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Even so they were condemned in their own time and became fodder for later debate.

sentences.zh: 若立廟大內而親享之，從古以來未有也。

translations.literal: To establish a temple within the Inner Palace and personally perform sacrifice—from antiquity to the present there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: To build a temple in the Inner Palace and sacrifice there in person—nothing like this has ever existed.

sentences.zh: 臣等寧得罪陛下，不欲陛下失禮於天下後世。

translations.literal: Your servants would rather offend Your Majesty than see Your Majesty lose ritual propriety before the realm and posterity.
translations.idiomatic: We would rather offend Your Majesty than see you violate ritual propriety before the world and posterity.

sentences.zh: 今張璁、桂萼之言曰『繼統公，立後私』。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Cong and Gui E say, "Succession to the lineage is public; establishing an heir is private."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E now say, "Succession to the lineage is a public matter; establishing an heir is private."

sentences.zh: 又曰『統為重，嗣為輕』。

translations.literal: They also say, "The lineage is weighty; the heirship is light."
translations.idiomatic: They also say, "The succession is paramount; heirship is secondary."

sentences.zh: 竊惟正統所傳之謂宗，故立宗所以繼統，立嗣所以承宗，統之與宗初無輕重。

translations.literal: We privately consider that what the orthodox succession transmits is called the ancestral lineage; therefore establishing the lineage is to continue the succession, and establishing an heir is to carry on the lineage—the succession and the lineage from the first have no weight or lightness.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that what the orthodox succession transmits is the ancestral lineage; to establish the lineage is to continue the succession, and to establish an heir is to sustain the lineage—succession and lineage were never unequal in weight.

sentences.zh: 況當我朝傳子之世，而欲仿堯、舜傳賢之例，擬非其倫。

translations.literal: Moreover, in our dynasty's age of transmitting the throne to sons, to imitate the example of Yao and Shun in transmitting to the worthy is to compare unlike categories.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in an age when our dynasty passes the throne from father to son, to imitate Yao and Shun's transfer to the worthy is to force an inapt analogy.

sentences.zh: 又謂『孝不在皇不皇，惟在考不考』，遂欲改稱孝宗為『皇伯考』。

translations.literal: They also say, "Filial piety lies not in whether one is emperor, but in whether one is father," and thereupon wish to change Xiaozong's title to "Imperial Uncle-Father."
translations.idiomatic: They also say, "Filial piety depends not on imperial rank but on fatherhood," and would retitle Xiaozong as "Imperial Uncle-Father."

sentences.zh: 臣等歷稽前古，未有神主稱『皇伯考』者。
