translations.literal: Your servants have examined all antiquity and found no spirit tablet titled "Imperial Uncle-Father."
translations.idiomatic: We have searched antiquity and found no spirit tablet ever titled "Imperial Uncle-Father."

sentences.zh: 惟天子稱諸王曰『伯叔父』則有之，非可加於宗廟也。

translations.literal: Only when the Son of Heaven addresses princes does he say "uncle and father"—that exists, but it may not be applied in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Heaven address princes as "uncle" or "father" in speech, but such terms cannot be placed in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 前此稱本生皇考，實裁自聖心。

translations.literal: The earlier title of Imperial Father of the birth parent was in truth trimmed by the sagely heart.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier title "Imperial Father of the birth parent" was in truth the emperor's own measured decision.

sentences.zh: 乃謂臣等留一皇字以覘陛下，又謂『百皇字不足當父子之名』，何肆言無忌至此。

translations.literal: Yet they say your servants kept one character "Imperial" to spy on Your Majesty, and also say, "A hundred characters 'Imperial' cannot equal the name of father and son"—how reckless and unbridled their words have become.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they accuse us of keeping the character "Imperial" to test Your Majesty, and say "a hundred times 'Imperial' cannot equal the bond of father and son"—how brazen their speech has become.

sentences.zh: 乞速罷建室之議，立廟安陸，下璁、萼等法司按治。」

translations.literal: We beg that the deliberation to build the chamber be quickly halted, a temple be established at Anlu, and Cong, E, and others be sent down to the judicial offices for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to halt the plan for the new chamber at once, build the temple at Anlu, and refer Cong, E, and their allies to the judicial authorities for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「朕起親藩，奉宗祀豈敢違越。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied: "We rose from a princely fief; how would we dare violate or overstep in serving the ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "I rose from a princely fief; how could I dare violate the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 但本生皇考寢園，遠在安陸，於卿等安乎？

translations.literal: But the burial park of the Imperial Father of the birth parent lies far away at Anlu—are you at ease with that?
translations.idiomatic: But my birth father's tomb lies far away at Anlu—are you content with that?

sentences.zh: 命下再四，爾等欺朕沖歲，黨同執違，敗父子之情，傷君臣之義。

translations.literal: Orders have been issued again and again; you deceive Us in Our tender years, band together and stubbornly disobey, ruin the feeling between father and son, and wound the righteousness between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: I have issued the order again and again; you take advantage of my youth, band together in defiance, ruin the bond between father and son, and wound the righteousness between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 往且勿問，其奉先殿西室亟修葺，盡朕歲時追遠之情。」

translations.literal: For now let that pass; quickly repair the western chamber of the Hall for Venerating Ancestors and fulfill Our feeling of annual remembrance and longing for the distant past."
translations.idiomatic: Let that go for now; repair the western chamber of the Hall for Venerating Ancestors at once, so I may fulfill my annual longing for my father.

sentences.zh: 時嘉靖三年四月也。

translations.literal: It was the fourth month of the third year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the fourth month of Jiajing 3.

sentences.zh: 頃之，一鵬極陳四方災異，言：「自去年六月迄今二月，其間天鳴者三，地震者三十八，秋冬雷電雨雹十八，暴風、白氣、地裂、山崩、產妖各一，民饑相食二。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, Yipeng urgently set forth the calamities and prodigies of the four quarters, saying: "From the sixth month of last year until the second month of this year, in that interval heaven sounded three times, the earth quaked thirty-eight times, thunder, lightning, rain, and hail in autumn and winter eighteen times, violent wind, white vapor, earth fissure, mountain collapse, and prodigious births each once, and the people starving and eating one another twice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Wu Yipeng urgently catalogued calamities across the realm: "From the sixth month of last year through the second month of this year, heaven sounded three times, the earth quaked thirty-eight times, there were eighteen episodes of thunder, lightning, rain, and hail in autumn and winter, and one each of violent wind, white vapor, earth fissure, mountain collapse, and monstrous births, while famine drove people to cannibalism twice.

sentences.zh: 非常之變，倍於往時。

translations.literal: Extraordinary changes exceed those of former times.
translations.idiomatic: Such extraordinary omens exceed those of any previous age.

sentences.zh: 願陛下率先群工，救疾苦，罷營繕，信大臣，納忠諫，用回天意。」

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to take the lead before all officials, relieve suffering and hardship, halt construction works, trust great ministers, accept loyal remonstrance, and thereby turn back Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to lead the officials, relieve suffering, halt construction, trust your senior ministers, accept loyal counsel, and turn back Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔報之。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied with an edict of gracious acknowledgment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 逾月，手敕名奉先殿西室為觀德殿，遂命一鵬偕中官賴義、京山侯崔元迎獻帝神主於安陸。

translations.literal: After more than a month, by handwritten edict he named the western chamber of the Hall for Venerating Ancestors the Guande Hall, and thereupon ordered Yipeng together with the eunuch Lai Yi and Marquis of Jingshan Cui Yuan to welcome the spirit tablet of the Xian emperor from Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, by personal edict he named the western chamber of the Hall for Venerating Ancestors the Guande Hall and ordered Wu Yipeng, the eunuch Lai Yi, and Marquis of Jingshan Cui Yuan to fetch the Prince of Xing's spirit tablet from Anlu.

sentences.zh: 一鵬等復上言：「歷考前史，並無自寢園迎主入大內者。

translations.literal: Yipeng and others again submitted, saying: "Examining all former histories, nowhere is there a case of welcoming a spirit tablet from a burial park into the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yipeng and his colleagues protested again: "No precedent in history shows a spirit tablet brought from a tomb park into the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 此天下後世觀瞻所系，非細故也。

translations.literal: This is what the gaze of the realm and posterity is fixed upon—not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: This bears on how the realm and posterity will judge you—not a minor matter.

sentences.zh: 且安陸為恭穆啟封之疆，神靈所戀，又陛下龍興之地，王氣所鐘。

translations.literal: Moreover, Anlu is the territory where Gongmu first received enfeoffment, where the numinous spirit dwells in attachment, and also the place where Your Majesty's dragon arose, where royal qi is concentrated.
translations.idiomatic: Anlu is the land where Gongmu first received his fief, where his spirit still dwells, and where Your Majesty's dragon first rose—the seat of royal qi.

sentences.zh: 故我太祖重中都，太宗重留都，皆以王業所基，永修世祀。

translations.literal: Therefore our Taizu valued the Central Capital and our Taizong valued the Preserved Capital—both because they were the base of royal enterprise, forever maintaining sacrifices for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperor valued Fengyang and our Yongle emperor valued Nanjing—both as foundations of the dynasty where sacrifices would endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 伏乞陛下俯納群言，改題神主，奉安故宮，為百世不遷。

translations.literal: We humbly beg Your Majesty to bow to and accept the multitude's words, retitle the spirit tablet, and install it in the former palace as a temple not to be moved for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg Your Majesty to accept the court's counsel, retitle the tablet, and enshrine it in the original palace as a temple fixed for all generations.

sentences.zh: 其觀德殿中別設神位香幾以慰孝思，則本生之情既隆，正統之義亦盡。」

translations.literal: Within the Guande Hall, separately set up a spirit seat and incense table to comfort filial longing—then the feeling toward the birth parent is exalted and the righteousness of the orthodox succession is also fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Set a separate spirit seat and incense table in the Guande Hall to comfort your filial longing—thus honoring your birth father while preserving the orthodox succession.

sentences.zh: 奏入，不納。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 一鵬乃行。

translations.literal: Yipeng then set out on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yipeng proceeded on the mission.

sentences.zh: 慮使者為道途患，疏請禁約，帝善其言而戒飭之。

translations.literal: Fearing that the envoys might become a scourge on the road, he memorialized requesting prohibitions and restrictions; the Emperor approved his words and issued warnings and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the mission might harass the countryside, he asked for strict regulations; the emperor approved and issued warnings.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，一鵬以本官入內閣專典誥敕兼掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, Yipeng entered the Grand Secretariat in his former capacity, exclusively managing edicts and concurrently directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That September, Wu Yipeng entered the Grand Secretariat in his existing rank, charged solely with drafting edicts while also overseeing the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 《武宗實錄》成，進尚書，領職如故。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Record of Wuzong was completed, he was advanced to Minister but retained his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Record of Emperor Wuzong was completed, he was promoted to Minister while keeping his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 尋以省墓歸，還朝仍典誥敕。

translations.literal: Shortly he returned to court on leave to tend his parents' graves and, upon returning, still managed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took leave to tend his family's graves, then returned to court and continued drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出理部事。

translations.literal: Before long, he went out to handle ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out to handle ministry business.

sentences.zh: 前此典內閣誥敕者，皆需次柄政。

translations.literal: Those who had previously managed edicts within the Grand Secretariat all awaited their turn to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had held the edict-drafting post in the Grand Secretariat traditionally awaited their turn at chief power.

sentences.zh: 而張璁、桂萼新用事，素銜一鵬異己，乃出為南京吏部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: But Zhang Cong and Gui E had newly come to power and long resented Yipeng for differing from them; they therefore sent him out as Minister of Personnel in Nanjing, with the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E had just risen to power and long resented Wu's opposition; they sent him to Nanjing as Minister of Personnel with the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 居二年，南京官劾諸大臣王瓊等不職，一鵬與焉，遂乞致仕。

translations.literal: After two years in office, Nanjing officials impeached various great ministers including Wang Qiong for dereliction; Yipeng was among them, and he thereupon requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, Nanjing officials impeached several senior ministers including Wang Qiong for incompetence; Wu was named among them and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 給廩如故事。

translations.literal: Grain allowance was granted according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted grain allowance according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 卒贈太子太保，謚文端。

translations.literal: Upon death he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous title was Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 子子孝，湖廣參政。

translations.literal: His son Zixiao became Administrative Commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixiao served as Administrative Commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 朱希周，字懋忠，昆山人，徙吳縣。

translations.literal: Zhu Xizhou, style Maozhong, a native of Kunshan who moved to Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou, whose style name was Maozhong, was born in Kunshan and later moved to Wu County.

sentences.zh: 高祖吉，戶科給事中。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ji was a supervising secretary in the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ji had been a supervising secretary in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 父文雲，按察副使。

translations.literal: His father Wenyun was a Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenyun was a Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 希周舉弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: Xizhou passed the metropolitan examination of Hongzhi 9.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 孝宗喜其姓名，擢為第一。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was pleased with his name and style and placed him first.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong was pleased with his name and style and ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，進侍講，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviser, advanced to Court Lecturer, and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed reviser, promoted to Court Lecturer, and served on the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾摘修《會典》小疵，降修撰。

translations.literal: Liu Jin seized upon minor flaws in the compilation of the Comprehensive Institutions and demoted him to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin seized on minor flaws in the compilation of the Comprehensive Institutions and demoted him to reviser.

sentences.zh: 《孝宗實錄》成，復官。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Record of Xiaozong was completed, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Record of Emperor Xiaozong was completed, his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 久之，進侍讀學士，擢南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was advanced to Lecturing Academician and promoted to Vice Minister of the right in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Lecturing Academician and promoted to Vice Minister of the right in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 閱五年，召為禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After five years he was summoned as Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was summoned as Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時方議「大禮」，數偕其長爭執。

translations.literal: At that time the "Great Rites" were under deliberation; repeatedly he joined his superior in struggle.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Rites were then under debate; he repeatedly joined his superior in protest.

sentences.zh: 會左侍郎吳一鵬奉使安陸，尚書席書未至，希周獨理部事。

translations.literal: It happened that Left Vice Minister Wu Yipeng was on a mission to Anlu, Minister Xi Shu had not yet arrived, and Xizhou alone handled Ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, Left Vice Minister Wu Yipeng was away on a mission to Anlu and Minister Xi Shu had not yet arrived; Zhu Xizhou handled Ministry affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 而帝方營觀德殿，令協律郎崔元初習樂舞生於大內。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Emperor was building Guande Hall and ordered Law-Coordinator Cui Yuanchu to train music-and-dance students within the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was meanwhile constructing Guande Hall and ordered Law-Coordinator Cui Yuanchu to train music-and-dance students inside the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 太常卿汪舉劾之。

translations.literal: Director of Court Ceremonies Wang Ju impeached this.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Court Ceremonies Wang Ju memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 帝遂令太常官一人同入內教習。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered one Court of Ceremonies official to enter together and teach and drill them inside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered one Court of Ceremonies official to enter the Inner Palace with him to oversee the training.

sentences.zh: 希周上言：「太常樂舞有定數，不當更設。」

translations.literal: Xizhou submitted, saying: "Court of Ceremonies music and dance have fixed numbers; they should not be additionally established."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou submitted: "The Court of Ceremonies has fixed quotas for music and dance; they ought not be expanded.

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 舉復爭，帝責其妄議。

translations.literal: Ju again contended; the Emperor rebuked him for reckless deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju protested again; the emperor rebuked him for reckless meddling.

sentences.zh: 而是時張璁、桂萼已召至，益交章請去本生之號。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Zhang Cong and Gui E had been summoned; all the more they submitted memorials in succession asking to remove the "birth parent" designation.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Cong and Gui E had been summoned to court and began submitting memorial after memorial demanding removal of the "birth parent" designation.

sentences.zh: 帝悅從之，趣禮官具上冊儀。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased to follow them and urged the Rites officials to prepare the investiture rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly assented and pressed the Rites officials to prepare the investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 希周率郎中余才、汪必東等疏諫曰：「陛下考孝宗、母昭聖三年矣，而更定之論忽從中出，則明詔為虛文，不足信天下，祭告為瀆禮，何以感神祇。

translations.literal: Xizhou led Bureau Directors Yu Cai, Wang Bidong, and others in a remonstrance, saying: "Your Majesty has treated Xiaozong as father and Zhaosheng as mother for three years, yet the theory of redefining terms suddenly issues from within—then the explicit edicts become empty words, insufficient to be trusted by the realm; sacrifices and announcements become impious rites—how could they move the spirits?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou led Bureau Directors Yu Cai, Wang Bidong, and others in a memorial of remonstrance: "Your Majesty has honored Emperor Xiaozong as father and Empress Zhaosheng as mother for three years; now this sudden reversal from within would render your clear edicts hollow words, unworthy of the realm's trust, and turn sacrifices and proclamations into profane rites—how could they move the spirits?

sentences.zh: 且本生非貶詞也，不妨正統，而親之義寓焉。

translations.literal: Moreover "birth parent" is not a derogatory term; it does not impede the orthodox succession, and the meaning of kinship is embodied in it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover "birth parent" is no term of disparagement; it does not compromise the orthodox succession, and the bond of kinship is implicit in it.

sentences.zh: 何嫌於此，而必欲去之，以滋天下之議。」

translations.literal: What scruple is there about this, that you must remove it and thereby multiply discussion throughout the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Why fix on this and insist on removing it, thereby multiplying controversy throughout the realm?

sentences.zh: 時群臣諫者甚眾，疏皆留中，遂相率詣左順門跪伏。

translations.literal: At that time remonstrating officials were extremely numerous; all memorials were retained at court; then they led one another to the Left Shun Gate and knelt prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: By then many officials had remonstrated; their memorials were all held at court without response, so they went in a body to the Left Shun Gate and knelt in protest.

sentences.zh: 希周走告諸閣臣曰：「群臣伏闕，公等能坐視乎？」

translations.literal: Xizhou ran to tell the Grand Secretaries, saying: "The ministers are prostrate at the gate—can you gentlemen sit and watch?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou rushed to tell the Grand Secretaries: "The ministers are kneeling at the palace gate—can you simply sit and watch?

sentences.zh: 亦偕群臣跪伏以請。

translations.literal: He too joined the ministers in kneeling prostrate to petition.
translations.idiomatic: He too joined the kneeling ministers in their petition.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，大怒，命希周與何孟春等俱待罪，而盡系庶僚於詔獄。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he was greatly enraged, ordered Xizhou and He Mengchun and others all to await punishment, and imprisoned all the lower officials in the Imperial Prison.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor he flew into a rage, ordered Zhu Xizhou and He Mengchun and the rest to await punishment, and had all the junior officials thrown into the Imperial Prison.

sentences.zh: 明日，上章聖皇太后冊文，希周及尚書秦金、金獻民、趙鑒、趙璜，侍郎何孟春，都御史王時中，大理少卿張縉、徐文華俱不赴。

translations.literal: The next day, when the investiture text for Empress Zhangsheng was presented, Xizhou and Ministers Qin Jin, Jin Xianmin, Zhao Jian, Zhao Huang, Vice Minister He Mengchun, Censor-in-chief Wang Shizhong, and Grand Court of Judicature Vice Directors Zhang Jin and Xu Wenhua all did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the investiture edict for Empress Zhangsheng was to be promulgated, Zhu Xizhou, Ministers Qin Jin, Jin Xianmin, Zhao Jian, and Zhao Huang, Vice Minister He Mengchun, Censor-in-chief Wang Shizhong, and Grand Court Vice Directors Zhang Jin and Xu Wenhua all refused to attend.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責陳狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and ordered them to state their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demanded they state their offenses.

sentences.zh: 希周等伏罪，復嚴旨譙責乃已。

translations.literal: Xizhou and others confessed guilt; only after stern edicts rebuking them did it end.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou and the others confessed their guilt; only after stern edicts of rebuke did the matter close.

sentences.zh: 而是時庶僚系獄者猶未釋，希周上言：「諸臣狂率，固不可宥。

translations.literal: Yet the lower officials still imprisoned had not been released; Xizhou submitted, saying: "The ministers were rash and reckless—truly they cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the junior officials still held in prison had not been released; Zhu Xizhou submitted: "Those ministers were rash and reckless and truly cannot be wholly excused.

sentences.zh: 但今獻皇帝神主將至，必百官齋迎，乃克成禮。

translations.literal: But now the spirit tablet of Emperor Xian is about to arrive; all officials must fast and receive it—only then can the rite be completed.
translations.idiomatic: But the spirit tablet of Emperor Xian is now approaching; all officials must purify themselves and receive it—only then can the ceremony be completed.

sentences.zh: 乞早寬縲絏，用襄大典。」

translations.literal: I beg early release from shackles to help fulfill the great ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that their bonds be loosened early so they may assist in this great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The plea was rejected.

sentences.zh: 「大禮」遂自此定矣。

translations.literal: The "Great Rites" were thereby settled from this point.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Rites controversy was thereby settled—from this point on.

sentences.zh: 其明年，由左侍郎遷南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred from Left Vice Minister to Nanjing Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted from Left Vice Minister to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，大計京官，南六科無黜者。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 6, at the great assessment of capital officials, none of the six Nanjing censorate sections were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing, during the grand assessment of capital officials, not a single post in the six Nanjing censorate sections was vacated.

sentences.zh: 桂萼素以議禮嗛希周，且惡兩京言官嘗劾己，因言希周畏勢曲庇。

translations.literal: Gui E had long resented Xizhou over the Rites deliberation and also hated that censors of both capitals had once impeached him; he therefore said Xizhou feared power and bent to shield them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E had long borne a grudge against Zhu Xizhou over the Rites controversy and also hated that censors in both capitals had once impeached him; he therefore charged that Zhu Xizhou feared power and had bent the rules to shield them.

sentences.zh: 希周言：「南京六科止七人，實無可去者。

translations.literal: Xizhou said: "The six Nanjing sections have only seven men—truly there is none who can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xizhou replied: "The six Nanjing sections have only seven men in all—there is truly no one who ought to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 臣以言路私之固不可，如避言路嫌，誅責之，尤不可。

translations.literal: Your servant using the remonstrance avenue for private ends indeed cannot be done; but to avoid the suspicion of the remonstrance avenue and punish and blame them is even more impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: To show favor through the remonstrance avenue would indeed be wrong; but to punish them merely to avoid the suspicion of favoritism would be even worse.

sentences.zh: 且使舉曹皆賢，必去一二人示公，設舉曹皆不肖，亦但去一二人塞責乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the entire staff were worthy, must one or two be removed to show fairness? Suppose the entire staff were unworthy—would one also remove only one or two to cover responsibility?"
translations.idiomatic: If the entire staff were worthy, must one or two still be dismissed to prove impartiality? And if the entire staff were unworthy, would dismissing only one or two suffice as accountability?

sentences.zh: 因力稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: Thereupon he strongly pleaded illness and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness in earnest and requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 溫旨許之，仍敕有司歲給夫廩。

translations.literal: A gracious edict permitted it, yet still ordered the relevant offices to supply bearers and grain rations yearly.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict granted his request, yet still ordered the relevant offices to supply bearers and grain rations each year.

sentences.zh: 林居三十年，中外論薦者三十余疏，竟不復起。

translations.literal: He dwelt in retirement thirty years; inside and outside, over thirty memorials recommending him—he was never recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for thirty years; more than thirty memorials recommending him arrived from within and without the court, yet he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，不妄取予。

translations.literal: His nature was respectful and careful; he did not take or give recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was respectful and circumspect and would take or accept nothing improperly.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十有四。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 瀕歿，屬諸子曰：「他日倘蒙易名典，勿犯我家諱。」

translations.literal: On the verge of death he charged his sons, saying: "If someday you receive the grace of a posthumous name according to statute, do not violate our family taboo."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he charged his sons: "If someday you receive the grace of a posthumous title by statute, do not violate our family's naming taboo.

sentences.zh: 乃避「文」，謚恭靖。

translations.literal: Thereupon avoiding "Wen," his posthumous name was Gongjing (Respectful and Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name accordingly avoided the character wen and he was styled Gongjing, "Respectful and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 何孟春，字子元，郴州人。

translations.literal: He Mengchun, style Ziyuan, a native of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun, whose style name was Ziyuan, was a native of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖俊，雲南按察司僉事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun had been an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父說，刑部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Yue was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue had been a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 孟春少遊李東陽之門，學問該博。

translations.literal: Mengchun in youth traveled in Li Dongyang's circle; his learning was comprehensive and broad.
translations.idiomatic: In youth He Mengchun studied under Li Dongyang; his learning was comprehensive and far-ranging.

sentences.zh: 第弘治六年進士，授兵部主事。

translations.literal: He placed among the Hongzhi 6 metropolitan graduates and was appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of Hongzhi and was appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 言官龐泮等下獄，疏救之。

translations.literal: When remonstrance officials Pang Pan and others were imprisoned, he memorialized to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrance officials Pang Pan and others were imprisoned, he submitted a memorial to secure their release.

sentences.zh: 詔修萬歲山毓秀亭、乾清宮西室，役軍九千人，計費百余萬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered repair of the Yuxiu Pavilion on Wansui Hill and the western chamber of Qianqing Palace, using nine thousand soldiers, estimated cost over a million.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered repairs to the Yuxiu Pavilion on Wansui Hill and the western chamber of Qianqing Palace, conscripting nine thousand soldiers at an estimated cost of over a million taels.

sentences.zh: 抗疏極諫。

translations.literal: He submitted a defiant memorial of utmost remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 清寧宮災，陳八事，疏萬余言。

translations.literal: When Qingning Palace burned, he set forth eight matters in a memorial of over ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingning Palace burned, he set forth eight proposals in a memorial of more than ten thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎、郎中，出理陜西馬政，條目畢張。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Bureau Vice Director and Director, went out to manage Shaanxi horse administration, and every regulation was fully deployed.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Bureau Vice Director and then Director, went out to administer Shaanxi horse policy, and implemented every regulation in full.

sentences.zh: 還，上厘弊五事，並劾撫臣不職。

translations.literal: On return he submitted five matters for correcting abuses and also impeached the Grand Coordinator for dereliction.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted five proposals for correcting abuses and also impeached the Grand Coordinator for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 正德初，請厘正孔廟祀典，不果行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he requested rectification of the Confucian temple sacrificial canon; it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he petitioned to rectify the Confucian temple sacrificial canon; the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 出為河南參政，廉公有威。

translations.literal: He went out as Administration Commissioner of Henan—incorrupt, fair, and commanding.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administration Commissioner of Henan, where he was incorruptible, impartial, and commanding.

sentences.zh: 擢太仆少卿，進為卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then advanced to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and then to Director.

sentences.zh: 駕幸宣府，馳疏諫。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession visited Xuanfu, he sent a rapid memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Xuanfu, he dispatched an urgent memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 尋以右副都御史巡撫雲南。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 討平十八寨叛蠻阿勿、阿寺等，奏設永昌府，增五長官司、五守禦所。

translations.literal: He suppressed the rebellious barbarians Afu, Asi, and others of the Eighteen Stockades, memorialized to establish Yongchang Prefecture, and added five native chieftain offices and five guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the rebel tribesmen Afu, Asi, and others of the Eighteen Stockades, memorialized to establish Yongchang Prefecture, and added five native chieftain offices and five guard posts.

sentences.zh: 錄功，蔭一子，辭不受。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; enfeoffment of one son was granted—he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and hereditary privilege for one son was granted; he declined and would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷南京兵部右侍郎，半道召為吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne he was transferred to Nanjing Vice Minister of War; halfway he was summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne he was transferred to Vice Minister of War at Nanjing; en route he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會蘇、松諸府旱潦相繼，而江、淮北河水大溢，漂沒田廬人畜無算。

translations.literal: It happened that drought and flood followed one another in the Su-Song prefectures, while north of the Jiang and Huai the river waters greatly overflowed, drowning fields, dwellings, livestock, and people beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and flood struck the Su and Song prefectures in succession, while north of the Yangzi and Huai the rivers burst their banks, drowning fields, homes, livestock, and people beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 孟春仿漢魏相條奏八事，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Mengchun, imitating Wei Xiang of Han, listed and submitted eight items; the Emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun, following the example of Wei Xiang of Han, submitted eight proposals in listed form; the emperor praised and adopted them.

sentences.zh: 尋進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 尚書喬宇罷，代署部事。

translations.literal: When Minister Qiao Yu was dismissed, he acted in his stead to handle Ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Qiao Yu was dismissed, He Mengchun acted in his stead and handled Ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，「大禮」議起。

translations.literal: Earlier, the "Great Rites" deliberation had arisen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Great Rites controversy had erupted.

sentences.zh: 孟春在雲南聞之，上疏言：

translations.literal: Mengchun heard of it in Yunnan and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun heard of it while in Yunnan and submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣閱邸報，見進士屈儒奏中請尊聖父為「皇叔考興獻大王」，聖母為「皇叔母興獻大王妃」。

translations.literal: Your servant has read the court gazette and seen in metropolitan graduate Qu Ru's memorial a request to honor the Sagely Father as "Imperial Uncle-Father, King Xingxian the Great," and the Sagely Mother as "Imperial Uncle-Mother, consort of King Xingxian the Great."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has read the court gazette and seen in metropolitan graduate Qu Ru's memorial a request to honor the Sagely Father as "Imperial Uncle-Father, King Xingxian the Great," and the Sagely Mother as "Imperial Uncle-Mother, consort of King Xingxian the Great."

sentences.zh: 得旨下部，知猶未奉俞命也。

translations.literal: An edict was obtained and sent down to the departments; I know the assenting command has not yet been received.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued and sent down to the ministries; I understand that assent has not yet been formally granted.

sentences.zh: 臣惟前世帝王，自旁支入奉大統，推尊本生，得失之跡具載史冊。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that former ages' emperors, entering the great succession from collateral branches and exalting their birth parents—the traces of gain and loss are fully recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects that emperors of former ages who entered the great succession from collateral lines and exalted their birth parents—the record of what they gained and lost is fully set down in the histories.

sentences.zh: 宣帝不敢加號於史皇孫，光武不敢加號於南頓君，晉元帝不敢加號於恭王，抑情守禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han did not dare add a title to the Historical Emperor's Grandson; Guangwu did not dare add a title to the Lord of Nandun; Emperor Yuan of Jin did not dare add a title to Prince Gong—they restrained feeling and upheld rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han did not dare add a title to the Historical Emperor's Grandson; Guangwu did not dare add a title to the Lord of Nandun; Emperor Yuan of Jin did not dare add a title to Prince Gong—they restrained their feelings and upheld the rites.

sentences.zh: 宋司馬光所謂當時歸美，後世頌聖者也。

translations.literal: What Song's Sima Guang called gaining praise in their time and being extolled as sagely by later ages.
translations.idiomatic: These are what Sima Guang of Song called rulers who won praise in their own day and were extolled as sagely by posterity.

sentences.zh: 哀、安、桓、靈乃追尊其父祖，犯義侵禮。

translations.literal: Emperors Ai, An, Huan, and Ling then posthumously honored their fathers and grandfathers, violating righteousness and encroaching on rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Ai, An, Huan, and Ling posthumously honored their fathers and grandfathers, violating righteousness and encroaching upon the rites.

sentences.zh: 司馬光所謂取譏當時，見非後世者也。

translations.literal: What Sima Guang called drawing ridicule in their time and being condemned by later ages.
translations.idiomatic: These are what Sima Guang called rulers who drew ridicule in their own day and were condemned by posterity.

sentences.zh: 《儀禮·喪服》：「為人後者」《傳》曰：「何以三年也？

translations.literal: The Ceremonies: Mourning Dress — "One who becomes another's heir" — the Commentary says: "Why three years?
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonies of Rites, Mourning Dress: "One who becomes another's heir"—the Commentary asks: "Why three years?

sentences.zh: 受重者，必以尊服服之」。

translations.literal: One who receives the weight [of succession] must wear the honored mourning for it."
translations.idiomatic: Because one who receives the weight of succession must wear the highest grade of mourning for it."

sentences.zh: 「為人後者，為其父母報」，傳曰：「何以期也？

translations.literal: "One who becomes another's heir still mourns for his parents" — the Commentary says: "Why one year?
translations.idiomatic: "One who becomes another's heir still mourns for his parents"—the Commentary asks: "Why only one year?

sentences.zh: 不二斬也」，「重大宗者，降其小宗也」。

translations.literal: No second full mourning" — "one who elevates the great lineage lowers his lesser lineage."
translations.idiomatic: Because there cannot be two periods of the highest mourning"—"one who elevates the great lineage demotes his lesser lineage."

sentences.zh: 夫父母，天下莫隆焉。

translations.literal: For parents—nothing under Heaven is more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: For parents, nothing under Heaven is more exalted.

sentences.zh: 至繼大宗則殺其服，而移於所後之親，蓋名之不可以二也。

translations.literal: Yet upon inheriting the great lineage one reduces mourning and shifts it to the lineage one has succeeded—because names cannot be twofold.
translations.idiomatic: Yet upon inheriting the great lineage one reduces mourning and shifts it to the lineage one has succeeded—because one's designation cannot be twofold.

sentences.zh: 為人後者為之子，不敢復顧私親。

translations.literal: One who becomes another's heir becomes that person's son and dares not again look back to private kin.
translations.idiomatic: One who becomes another's heir becomes that person's son and dares not again turn back to private kin.

sentences.zh: 聖人制禮，尊無二上，若恭敬之心分於彼，則不得專於此故也。

translations.literal: The sages instituted rites—honor has no second apex; if reverent respect divides to that side, one cannot be wholehearted on this side—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: The sages instituted the rites: honor admits no second apex; if reverent devotion is divided toward another, it cannot be wholehearted here—that is the reason.

sentences.zh: 今者廷臣詳議，事獄未決，豈非皇叔考之稱有未當者乎？

translations.literal: Now the court ministers have deliberated in detail; the matter is not yet settled—can it be that the title Imperial Uncle-Father is inappropriate?
translations.idiomatic: Now the court ministers have deliberated at length, yet the matter remains unsettled—can it be that the title Imperial Uncle-Father is inappropriate?

sentences.zh: 抑臣愚亦不能無疑。

translations.literal: Or perhaps your servant's dullness also cannot be without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this humble servant's dull wit cannot help but harbor doubts as well.

sentences.zh: 《禮》，生曰「父母」，死曰「考妣」，有「世父母」、「叔父母」之文，而無世叔考、世叔妣之說。

translations.literal: In the Rites, while alive one says "parents"; after death "deceased father and mother"; there are texts for "paternal uncle and aunt" and "maternal uncle and aunt," but no doctrine of paternal imperial uncle-father or maternal imperial uncle-mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites, the living are called "parents" and the dead "deceased father and mother"; there are passages for "paternal uncle and aunt" and "maternal uncle and aunt," but no doctrine of Imperial Uncle-Father or Imperial Uncle-Mother.

sentences.zh: 今欲稱興獻王為皇叔考，古典何據？

translations.literal: Now wishing to style Prince Xingxian as Imperial Uncle-Father—what ancient classic is the authority?
translations.idiomatic: To style Prince Xingxian as Imperial Uncle-Father now—what ancient classic provides authority?

sentences.zh: 宋英宗時有請加濮王皇伯考者，宋敏求力斥其謬。

translations.literal: In Song, during Emperor Yingzong's time, some requested adding to Prince Pu the title Imperial Uncle-Father-once-removed; Song Minqiu forcefully rejected the error.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yingzong's reign in Song, some petitioned to add to Prince Pu the title Imperial Uncle-Father-once-removed; Song Minqiu forcefully rejected the error.

sentences.zh: 然則皇叔考之稱，豈可加於興獻王乎？

translations.literal: Then can the title Imperial Uncle-Father be added to Prince Xingxian?
translations.idiomatic: If so, how can the title Imperial Uncle-Father be applied to Prince Xingxian?

sentences.zh: 即稱皇叔父，於義亦未安也。

translations.literal: Even styling Imperial Uncle-Father—in principle it is still unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Even the title Imperial Uncle-Father would be improper in principle.

sentences.zh: 經書稱伯父、叔父皆生時相呼，及其既歿，從無通親屬冠於爵位之上者。

translations.literal: The classics call paternal and maternal uncles while alive; after death, never has kin terminology been placed atop ennoblement titles.
translations.idiomatic: The classics address paternal and maternal uncles only while they live; after death, kinship terms are never placed above ennobled titles.

sentences.zh: 然則皇叔父之稱，其可復加先朝已謚之親王乎？

translations.literal: Then can Imperial Uncle-Father again be added to a prince already given a posthumous title in the previous reign?
translations.idiomatic: How then can Imperial Uncle-Father be added to a prince already given a posthumous title under the previous reign?

sentences.zh: 臣伏睹前詔，陛下稱先皇帝為皇兄，誠於獻王稱皇叔，如宋王珪、司馬光所雲，亦已愜矣。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly sees the earlier edict: Your Majesty styled the former emperor as Imperial Elder Brother; truly to style Prince Xian as Imperial Uncle—as Song's Wang Gui and Sima Guang said—would already be satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly notes the earlier edict in which Your Majesty styled the former emperor as Imperial Elder Brother; to style Prince Xian as Imperial Uncle—as Wang Gui and Sima Guang of Song argued—would already be fully satisfactory.

sentences.zh: 而議者或不然，何也？

translations.literal: Yet some deliberators disagree—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet some in the debate demur—why?

sentences.zh: 天下者，太祖之天下也。

translations.literal: The realm is Taizu the Founder's realm.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is the realm of Taizu the Founder.

sentences.zh: 自太祖傳至孝宗，孝宗傳之先皇帝，特簡陛下，授之大業。

translations.literal: From Taizu it passed to Xiaozong, Xiaozong passed it to the former emperor, who specially selected Your Majesty and bestowed the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu it passed to Emperor Xiaozong, from Xiaozong to the former emperor, who specially selected Your Majesty and bestowed the great enterprise upon you.

sentences.zh: 獻王雖陛下天性至親，然而所以光臨九重，富有四海，子子孫孫萬世南面者，皆先皇帝之德，孝宗之所貽也。

translations.literal: Prince Xian, though by nature Your Majesty's closest kin—yet that by which you brightly preside over the Ninefold Gate, possess all within the Four Seas, and face south for ten thousand generations, sons and grandsons—all is the former emperor's virtue, what Xiaozong bequeathed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian, though by nature Your Majesty's closest kin, is not the source of your bright presence upon the Ninefold Gate, your possession of all within the Four Seas, or your facing south for ten thousand generations, sons and grandsons—that all derives from the former emperor's virtue and what Emperor Xiaozong bequeathed.

sentences.zh: 臣故願以漢宣、光武、晉元三帝為法，若非古之名，不正之號，非臣所願於陛下也。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore wishes to take the three emperors Xuan of Han, Guangwu, and Yuan of Jin as models; if not ancient names and not correct titles—they are not what your servant wishes upon Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant therefore urges Your Majesty to take as models the three emperors Xuan of Han, Guangwu, and Yuan of Jin; titles that are neither ancient in form nor correct in principle are not what your servant wishes for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 及孟春官吏部，則已尊本生父母為「興獻帝」、「興國太后」。

translations.literal: By the time Mengchun held office in the Ministry of Personnel, his birth parents had already been honored as "Emperor Xingxian" and "Empress Dowager of Xingguo."
translations.idiomatic: By the time He Mengchun took office in the Ministry of Personnel, his birth parents had already been honored as "Emperor Xingxian" and "Empress Dowager of Xingguo."

sentences.zh: 繼又改稱「本生皇考恭穆獻皇帝」、「本生聖母章聖皇太后」。

translations.literal: Then they were again changed to "Birth-Parent Imperial Deceased Father, Respectful and Solemn Emperor Xian" and "Birth-Parent Sagely Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng."
translations.idiomatic: They were then changed again to "Birth-Parent Imperial Deceased Father, Respectful and Solemn Emperor Xian" and "Birth-Parent Sagely Mother, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng."

sentences.zh: 孟春三上疏乞從初詔，皆不省。

translations.literal: Mengchun three times submitted asking to follow the initial edict—all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun submitted three memorials begging adherence to the initial edict; none received a response.

sentences.zh: 於是帝益入張璁、桂萼等言，復欲去本生二字。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor all the more took in Zhang Cong, Gui E, and others' words and again wished to remove the two characters "birth parent."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor all the more embraced the arguments of Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their allies and again sought to remove the two characters "birth parent."

sentences.zh: 璁方盛氣，列上禮官欺妄十三事，且斥為朋黨。

translations.literal: Cong was at the height of his arrogance, listing thirteen matters in which Rites officials deceived and falsely claimed, and moreover denounced them as a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong was riding a wave of arrogance, listing thirteen charges of deception and falsehood against the Rites officials and denouncing them as a faction.

sentences.zh: 孟春偕九卿秦金等具疏，略曰：「伊尹謂『有言逆於心，必求諸道。

translations.literal: Mengchun joined the Nine Ministers Qin Jin and others in preparing a memorial, briefly saying: "Yi Yin said: 'When words run counter to the heart, one must seek them in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun joined the Nine Ministers, including Qin Jin, in a joint memorial that began: "Yi Yin said: 'When words run counter to the heart, one must seek them in the Way.

sentences.zh: 有言遜於誌，必求諸非道』。

translations.literal: When words accord with one's wishes, one must seek them outside the Way.'"
translations.idiomatic: When words accord with one's wishes, one must seek them outside the Way.'"

sentences.zh: 邇者，大禮之議，邪正不同。

translations.literal: Recently, in the debate over the Great Rites, the orthodox and heterodox differ.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in the debate over the Great Rites, orthodox and heterodox positions have sharply diverged.

sentences.zh: 若諸臣匡拂，累千萬言，此所謂逆於心之言也，陛下亦嘗求諸道否乎？

translations.literal: As for the various ministers' remonstrances, they amount to tens of millions of words—this is what is called words running counter to the heart; has Your Majesty also sought them in the Way?
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers' remonstrances run to millions of words—they are precisely "words that run counter to the heart." Has Your Majesty ever tested them against the Way?

sentences.zh: 一二小人，敢托將順之說，招徠罷閑不學無恥之徒，熒惑聖聽，此所謂遜於誌之言也，陛下亦嘗求諸非道否乎？

translations.literal: One or two petty men dare rely on accommodating speech, recruit dismissed idlers who lack learning and shame, and dazzle the sage ear—this is what is called words accordant with wishes; has Your Majesty also sought them outside the Way?
translations.idiomatic: A handful of petty men dare peddle accommodating speech, recruit dismissed idlers devoid of learning or shame, and dazzle Your Majesty's ear—these are "words that accord with one's wishes." Has Your Majesty ever tested them against what lies outside the Way?

sentences.zh: 何彼言之易行，而此言之難入也。」

translations.literal: Why are those words easy to enact while these words hard to enter?"
translations.idiomatic: Why are the former so easily heeded while the latter cannot gain a hearing?

sentences.zh: 遂發十三難以辨折璁，疏入留中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised thirteen difficulties to refute Cong; the memorial entered and was held within.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial then laid out thirteen objections to refute Zhang Cong and was submitted, but held in abeyance at court.

sentences.zh: 其時詹事、翰林、給事、御史及六部諸司、大理、行人諸臣各具疏爭，並留中不下，群情益洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time the Household Tutor, Hanlin, supervising secretaries, censors, and officials of the Six Ministries, various departments, Court of Revision, and Traveling Clerks each prepared competing memorials, all held within and not issued; public sentiment grew ever more turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Household Tutor, Hanlin Academy, supervising secretaries, censors, and officials of the Six Ministries, their departments, the Court of Revision, and the Traveling Clerks each submitted competing memorials, all held in abeyance and not issued; public sentiment grew ever more turbulent.

sentences.zh: 會朝方罷，孟春倡言於眾曰：「憲宗朝，百官哭文華門，爭慈懿皇太后葬禮，憲宗從之，此國朝故事也。」

translations.literal: When the audience had just ended, Mengchun took the lead in addressing the crowd, saying: "In the Chenghua reign, the hundred officials wept at Wenhua Gate contending over Empress Dowager Ciyi's funeral rites, and Chenghua assented—this is a dynastic precedent."
translations.idiomatic: When the audience had just ended, He Mengchun took the lead in addressing the crowd: "In the Chenghua reign, the hundred officials wept at Wenhua Gate to contest Empress Dowager Ciyi's funeral rites, and Emperor Chenghua assented—that is a dynastic precedent.

sentences.zh: 修撰楊慎曰：「國家養士百五十年，仗節死義，正在今日。」

translations.literal: Compiler Yang Shen said: "The state has nurtured scholars for a hundred and fifty years; to hold to integrity and die for righteousness—that moment is today."
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Yang Shen said: "The state has nurtured scholars for a hundred and fifty years; to hold fast to integrity and die for righteousness—that moment is today.

sentences.zh: 編修王元正、給事中張翀等遂遮留群臣於金水橋南，謂今日有不力爭者，必共擊之。

translations.literal: Compiler Wang Yuanzheng, supervising secretary Zhang Chong, and others then blocked and detained the officials south of the Jinshui Bridge, declaring that whoever today did not strive with all his might would be jointly struck down.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Wang Yuanzheng, supervising secretary Zhang Chong, and others then blocked and detained the officials south of the Jinshui Bridge, declaring that anyone who today did not strive with all his might would be jointly struck down.

sentences.zh: 孟春、金獻民、徐文華復相號召。

translations.literal: Mengchun, Jin Xianmin, and Xu Wenhua again called upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun, Jin Xianmin, and Xu Wenhua again rallied one another.

sentences.zh: 於是九卿則尚書獻民及秦金、趙鑒、趙璜、俞琳、侍郎孟春及朱希周、劉玉，都御史王時中、張潤，寺卿汪舉、潘希曾、張九敘、吳祺，通政張瓚、陳霑，少卿徐文華及張縉、蘇民、金瓚，府丞張仲賢，通政參議葛禬，寺丞袁宗儒，凡二十有三人；

translations.idiomatic: Thus among the Nine Ministers: Ministers Jin Xianmin, Qin Jin, Zhao Jian, Zhao Huang, and Yu Lin; Vice Ministers He Mengchun, Zhu Xizhou, and Liu Yu; Censor-in-Chief Wang Shizhong and Zhang Run; Directors Wang Ju, Pan Xizeng, Zhang Jiuxu, and Wu Qi; Transmission Commissioners Zhang Zan and Chen Zhan; Junior Directors Xu Wenhua, Zhang Jin, Su Min, and Jin Zan; Prefectural Assistant Zhang Zhongxian; Transmission Vice Commissioner Ge Qi; and Court of Revision Assistant Yuan Zongru—twenty-three in all;
