translations.idiomatic: Court of Revision subordinates: Directors Mu Dechun and Jiang Tongren; Vice Directors Wang Wei and Liu Dao; Reviewers Chen Dagang, Zhong Yunrui, Wang Guangji, Zhang Hui, Wang Tianmin, Zheng Zhong, and Du Luan—eleven in all.

sentences.zh: 俱跪伏左順門。

translations.literal: All knelt prostrate at the Left Straight Gate.
translations.idiomatic: All knelt prostrate at the Left Straight Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝命司禮中官諭退，眾皆曰：「必得俞旨乃敢退。」

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Director of Ceremonial eunuchs to instruct them to withdraw; all said: "We dare withdraw only upon receiving Your Majesty's assent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Director of Ceremonial eunuchs to instruct them to withdraw; all said: "We dare withdraw only upon receiving Your Majesty's assent.

sentences.zh: 自辰至午，凡再傳諭，猶跪伏不起。

translations.literal: From the hour of chen to wu, twice orders were transmitted, yet they still knelt prostrate and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: From the hour of chen to wu, orders were transmitted twice, yet they still knelt prostrate and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遣錦衣先執為首者。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and sent Brocade Guards first to seize the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged and sent Brocade Guards first to seize the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 於是豐熙、張翀、余翺、余寬、黃待顯、陶滋、相世芳、母德純八人，並系詔獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng Xi, Zhang Chong, Yu Ao, Yu Kuan, Huang Daixian, Tao Zi, Xiang Shifang, and Mu Dechun—eight men—were all imprisoned by imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Feng Xi, Zhang Chong, Yu Ao, Yu Kuan, Huang Daixian, Tao Zi, Xiang Shifang, and Mu Dechun—eight men in all—were imprisoned by imperial command.

sentences.zh: 楊慎、王元正乃撼門大哭，眾皆哭，聲震闕廷。

translations.literal: Yang Shen and Wang Yuanzheng then shook the gate and wept loudly; all wept, and the sound shook the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen and Wang Yuanzheng then shook the gate and wept aloud; all wept, and the sound shook the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，命收系五品以下官若干人，而令孟春等待罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still more enraged, ordered the seizure and imprisonment of a number of officials below the fifth rank, and commanded Mengchun and others to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more enraged, ordered the seizure and imprisonment of a number of officials below the fifth rank, and commanded He Mengchun and others to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 翼日，編修王相等十八人俱杖死，熙等及慎、元正俱謫戍，始下孟春等前疏，責曰：「朕嗣承大統，祗奉宗廟，尊崇大禮，自出朕心。

translations.literal: The next day, Compiler Wang Xiang and seventeen others were all beaten to death; Xi and the others, together with Shen and Yuanzheng, were all banished to border garrison; only then were Mengchun and others' earlier memorials issued, with rebuke: "We have succeeded to the great succession, reverently tended the ancestral temples, and honored the Great Rites—this sprang from Our own heart.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, Compiler Wang Xiang and seventeen others were all beaten to death; Feng Xi and the others, together with Yang Shen and Wang Yuanzheng, were all banished to border garrison; only then were He Mengchun and others' earlier memorials issued, with rebuke: "We have succeeded to the great succession, reverently tended the ancestral temples, and honored the Great Rites—this sprang from Our own heart.

sentences.zh: 孟春等毀君害政，變亂是非。

translations.literal: Mengchun and others slandered the ruler and harmed government, confounding right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun and others slandered the ruler and harmed government, confounding right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 且張璁等所上十三條尚留中未發，安得先知？

translations.literal: Moreover, the thirteen items Zhang Cong and others submitted were still held within and unissued—how could you have known beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the thirteen items Zhang Cong and others submitted were still held in abeyance and unissued—how could you have known beforehand?

sentences.zh: 其以實對。」

translations.literal: Answer in truth."
translations.idiomatic: Answer in truth.

sentences.zh: 於是孟春等具疏伏罪，言：「璁等所條者，於未進之日先以私稿示人，且有副本存通政司，故臣等知之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mengchun and others prepared memorials confessing guilt, saying: "What Cong and others listed—before submission they had already shown private drafts to others, and copies were stored at the Office of Transmission, hence your servants knew.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon He Mengchun and others prepared memorials confessing guilt, saying: "What Zhang Cong and others listed—before submission they had already shown private drafts to others, and copies were stored at the Office of Transmission, hence your servants knew.

sentences.zh: 臣等忝從大臣後，得與議禮之末。

translations.literal: Your servants humbly followed behind the great ministers and were permitted to take part at the end of Rites deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants humbly followed behind the great ministers and were permitted to take part at the end of Rites deliberations.

sentences.zh: 竊以璁等欺罔，故昌言論辨，以瀆天聽，罪應萬死。

translations.literal: We privately judged Cong and others to be deceitful, hence spoke boldly in debate to profane Heaven's hearing—crime deserving ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: We privately judged Zhang Cong and others to be deceitful, hence spoke boldly in debate to profane Heaven's hearing—crime deserving ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 惟望聖明加察，辨其孰正孰邪，則臣等雖死亦幸。」

translations.literal: We only hope the sage brightness will add scrutiny and distinguish which is orthodox and which heterodox; then though your servants die, it would be fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: We only hope Your Majesty's sage brightness will add scrutiny and distinguish which is orthodox and which heterodox; then though your servants die, it would be fortunate.

sentences.zh: 帝怒不已，責孟春倡眾逞忿，非大臣事君之道，法宜重治，姑從輕奪俸一月。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger did not cease; he rebuked Mengchun for inciting the multitude and venting resentment, not the Way of a great minister serving his ruler—by law he should be severely punished, but for the moment leniently stripped one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger did not cease; he rebuked He Mengchun for inciting the multitude and venting resentment, not the Way of a great minister serving his ruler—by law he should be severely punished, but for the moment leniently stripped one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 旋出為南京工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred out as Left Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was transferred out as Left Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 故事，南部止侍郎一人，時已有右侍郎張琮，復以孟春為左，蓋賸員也。

translations.literal: By precedent the southern capital had only one vice minister; at the time there was already Right Vice Minister Zhang Cong; Mengchun was again made Left—essentially a supernumerary post.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the southern capital had only one vice minister; at the time there was already Right Vice Minister Zhang Cong; He Mengchun was again made Left—essentially a supernumerary post.

sentences.zh: 孟春屢疏引疾，至六年春始得請。

translations.literal: Mengchun repeatedly memorialized citing illness; only in the spring of the sixth year did he obtain leave.
translations.idiomatic: He Mengchun repeatedly memorialized citing illness; only in the spring of the sixth year did he obtain leave.

sentences.zh: 及《明倫大典》成，削其籍。

translations.literal: When the Canon of Bright Moral Relations was completed, his registry was struck.
translations.idiomatic: When the Canon of Bright Moral Relations was completed, his name was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long while he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he died at home.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈禮部尚書，謚文簡。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.

sentences.zh: 孟春所居有泉，用燕去來時盈涸得名，遂稱「燕泉先生」雲。

translations.literal: At Mengchun's residence there was a spring that rose and fell with the swallows' coming and going, hence he was styled "Master Yanquan."
translations.idiomatic: At He Mengchun's residence there was a spring that rose and fell with the swallows' coming and going, hence he was styled "Master Yanquan."

sentences.zh: 豐熙，字原學，鄞人，布政司慶孫也。

translations.literal: Feng Xi, style Yuanxue, a native of Yin, was grandson of Regional Commissioner Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi, style Yuanxue, a native of Yin, was grandson of Regional Commissioner Qing.

sentences.zh: 幼有異稟。

translations.literal: In youth he had unusual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he showed unusual gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗大書壁間曰：「立誌當以聖人為的。

translations.literal: Once he wrote large on his wall: "To set one's ambition, take the sages as one's target.
translations.idiomatic: Once he wrote large characters on his wall: "To set one's ambition, take the sages as one's target.

sentences.zh: 遜第一等事於人，非夫也。」

translations.literal: To yield first place to others is not the act of a real man."
translations.idiomatic: To yield first place to others is not the act of a real man.

sentences.zh: 年十六喪母，水漿不入口數日，居倚廬三年。

translations.literal: At sixteen he mourned his mother, took no water or gruel for several days, and dwelt in the mourning hut three years.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he mourned his mother, took no water or gruel for several days, and dwelt in the mourning hut three years.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年舉殿試第二。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he placed second in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he placed second in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 孝宗奇其策，賜第一人袍帶寵之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong marveled at his examination essay and bestowed upon him the first-place scholar's robe and sash as a special honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong marveled at his examination essay and bestowed upon him the first-place scholar's robe and sash as a special honor.

sentences.zh: 授編修，進侍講，遷右諭德。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler, advanced to Lecturer, and transferred to Right Instructor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Compiler, advanced to Lecturer, and transferred to Right Instructor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以不附劉瑾，出掌南京翰林院事。

translations.literal: Because he would not attach himself to Liu Jin, he was sent out to direct affairs of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Because he would not attach himself to Liu Jin, he was sent out to direct affairs of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 父喪闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his father ended, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 既璁等得誌，乃相率請釋謫戍諸臣罪，皆首及熙，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Once Cong and others had their way, they jointly pleaded to release the guilt of banished officials, all naming Xi first; the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Cong and others had their way, they jointly pleaded to release the guilt of banished officials, all naming Feng Xi first; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 最後謹身殿災，熙年且七十，給事中田濡復請矜宥，卒不聽。

translations.literal: Finally when the Jinshen Hall burned, Xi was nearly seventy; supervising secretary Tian Ru again pleaded for compassion, but in the end the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Finally when the Jinshen Hall burned, Feng Xi was nearly seventy; supervising secretary Tian Ru again pleaded for compassion, but in the end the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 居十有三年，竟卒於戍所。

translations.literal: After dwelling there thirteen years, he finally died at the place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: After dwelling there thirteen years, he finally died at his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈官賜恤。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was given posthumous rank and mourning allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was given posthumous rank and mourning allowances.

sentences.zh: 子坊，字存禮。

translations.literal: His son Fang, style Cunli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng Fang, style Cunli.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: He topped the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年成進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he became a graduate of the advanced examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing he passed the advanced examination.

sentences.zh: 出為南京吏部考功主事。

translations.literal: He was sent out as section chief of Personnel Evaluation in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as section chief of Personnel Evaluation in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋謫通州同知。

translations.literal: Shortly he was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 免歸。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 坊博學工文，兼通書法，而性狂誕。

translations.literal: Fang was broadly learned and skilled in letters, and also versed in calligraphy, but by nature wild and eccentric.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fang was broadly learned and skilled in letters, and also versed in calligraphy, but by nature wild and eccentric.

sentences.zh: 熙既卒，家居貧乏，思效張璁、夏言片言取通顯。

translations.literal: After Xi had died, living at home in poverty, he sought to emulate Zhang Cong and Xia Yan—gaining swift advancement through a single remark.
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Xi had died, living at home in poverty, he sought to emulate Zhang Cong and Xia Yan—gaining swift advancement through a single remark.

sentences.zh: 十七年詣闕上書，言建明堂事，又言宜加獻皇帝廟號稱宗，從配上帝，世宗大悅。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he came to the capital and submitted a memorial on building the Bright Hall, and further argued that the posthumous temple name of Emperor Xian should be elevated to "Zong" and he should share sacrifice with the Lord on High; Shizong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he came to the capital and submitted a memorial on building the Bright Hall, and further argued that the posthumous temple name of Emperor Xian should be elevated to "Zong" and he should share sacrifice with the Lord on High; the Jiajing Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進號睿宗，配饗玄極殿。

translations.literal: Before long the posthumous title Ruizong was advanced, with joint sacrifice at the Profound Pole Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the posthumous title Ruizong was advanced, with joint sacrifice at the Profound Pole Hall.

sentences.zh: 其議蓋自坊始，人鹹惡坊畔父雲。

translations.literal: That policy essentially began with Fang; people all reviled Fang for turning against his father.
translations.idiomatic: That policy essentially began with Feng Fang; people all reviled him for turning against his father.

sentences.zh: 明年復進《卿雲雅詩》一章，詔付史館。

translations.literal: The next year he again presented a chapter of "Elegant Ode of Felicitous Clouds"; an edict ordered it delivered to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he again presented a chapter of "Elegant Ode of Felicitous Clouds"; an edict ordered it delivered to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 待命久之，竟無所進擢，歸家悒悒以卒。

translations.literal: Awaiting appointment a long while, ultimately with no advancement, he returned home and died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting appointment a long while, ultimately with no advancement, he returned home and died in dejection.

sentences.zh: 晚歲改名道生。

translations.literal: In his late years he changed his name to Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: In his late years he changed his name to Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 別為《十三經訓詁》，類多穿鑿語。

translations.literal: He separately compiled Exegesis of the Thirteen Classics, mostly forced interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: He separately compiled Exegesis of the Thirteen Classics, mostly forced interpretations.

sentences.zh: 或謂世所傳《子貢詩傳》，亦坊偽纂也。

translations.literal: Some say the Zi Gong Poetry Commentary transmitted in the world was also forged and compiled by Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the Zi Gong Poetry Commentary transmitted in the world was also forged and compiled by Feng Fang.

sentences.zh: 徐文華，字用光，嘉定州人。

translations.literal: Xu Wenhua, style Yongguang, a native of Jiading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenhua, style Yongguang, a native of Jiading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he became a graduate of the advanced examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengde he passed the advanced examination.

sentences.zh: 授大理評事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Reviewer at the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Reviewer at the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，巡按貴州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising censor and made an inspection tour of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor and made an inspection tour of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 乖西苗阿雜等倡亂，偕巡撫魏英討之，破寨六百三十。

translations.literal: The western Miao of Guaixi, Aza and others, raised rebellion; together with Grand Coordinator Wei Ying he attacked them and destroyed six hundred and thirty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The western Miao of Guaixi, Aza and others, raised rebellion; together with Grand Coordinator Wei Ying he attacked them and destroyed six hundred and thirty stockades.

sentences.zh: 璽書獎勞。

translations.literal: An imperial missive rewarded and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial missive rewarded and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 江西副使胡世寧坐論寧王宸濠系詔獄，文華抗疏救曰：「世寧上為聖朝，下為宗室，竭誠發憤，言甫脫口，而禍患隨之，亦可哀也。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Vice Commissioner Hu Shining was imprisoned by imperial command for discussing Prince of Ning Chen Hao; Wenhua submitted a bold memorial in rescue, saying: "Shining above serves the sage dynasty, below serves the imperial clan, exhausting sincerity and venting indignation—no sooner had the words left his mouth than calamity followed; this too is pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Vice Commissioner Hu Shining was imprisoned by imperial command for discussing Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao; Xu Wenhua submitted a bold memorial in his defense, saying: "Shining serves the sage dynasty above and the imperial clan below, exhausting sincerity and venting indignation—no sooner had the words left his mouth than calamity followed; this too is pitiable.

sentences.zh: 寧王威焰日以張，隱患日以甚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning's threatening aura grows daily more imposing; hidden peril grows daily more grave.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning's threatening aura grows daily more imposing; hidden peril grows daily more grave.

sentences.zh: 失今不戢，容有紀極。

translations.literal: If not checked now, there may be no limit.
translations.idiomatic: If not checked now, there may be no limit.

sentences.zh: 顧又置世寧重法，杜天下之口，奪忠鯁之氣，弱朝廷之勢，啟宗藩之心，招意外之變，皆自今日始矣。」

translations.literal: Yet again to impose heavy punishment on Shining, to stop the mouths of the realm, to drain the spirit of the loyal and forthright, to weaken the court's power, to open the hearts of the imperial clans, to invite unforeseen change—all begins from today."
translations.idiomatic: Yet again to impose heavy punishment on Shining, to stop the mouths of the realm, to drain the spirit of the loyal and forthright, to weaken the court's power, to open the hearts of the imperial clans, to invite unforeseen change—all begins from today.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: It was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官劉允迎佛烏斯藏，文華力諫。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched eunuch Liu Yun to welcome Buddhist [relics/images] from Ü-Tsang; Wenhua strongly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched eunuch Liu Yun to welcome Buddhist images from Ü-Tsang; Xu Wenhua strongly remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: No response.

sentences.zh: 馬昂納妊身女弟於帝，又疏諫曰：「中人之家不取再醮之婦。

translations.literal: Ma Ang took into the palace his pregnant younger sister; [Wenhua] again remonstrated in a memorial: "A middle-class family does not take a twice-married woman.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ang took into the palace his pregnant younger sister; Xu Wenhua again remonstrated in a memorial: "A middle-class family does not take a twice-married woman.

sentences.zh: 陛下萬乘至尊，乃有此舉，返之於心則不安，宣之於口則不順，傳之天下後世則可醜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, supreme sovereign of ten thousand chariots, yet has such an act—turned back upon the heart it is uneasy, spoken from the mouth it is inharmonious, transmitted to the realm and to later ages it is shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, supreme sovereign of ten thousand chariots, yet has such an act—turned back upon the heart it is uneasy, spoken from the mouth it is inharmonious, transmitted to the realm and to later ages it is shameful.

sentences.zh: 誰為陛下進此者，罪可族也。

translations.literal: Whoever advanced this to Your Majesty—his crime could extend to his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever advanced this to Your Majesty—his crime could extend to his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 萬一防閑闊略，不幸有李園、呂不韋之徒乘間投隙，豈細故哉。

translations.literal: If by chance precautions at the women's quarters were relaxed, and unhappily men such as Li Yuan or Lü Buwei seized the interval to slip in, would that be a trivial matter?
translations.idiomatic: If by chance precautions at the women's quarters were relaxed, and unhappily men such as Li Yuan or Lü Buwei seized the interval to slip in, would that be a trivial matter?

sentences.zh: 今昂兄弟子侄出入禁闥，陛下降絀等威，與之亂服雜坐，或同臥起，壞祖宗法，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Now Ang's brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law come and go within the forbidden gates; Your Majesty lowers cord and equal majesty, mingling with them in disorderly dress and sitting together, sometimes rising and lying down together—to destroy ancestral law, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ang's brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law come and go within the forbidden gates; Your Majesty lowers cord and equal majesty, mingling with them in disorderly dress and sitting together, sometimes rising and lying down together—to destroy ancestral law, nothing surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 馬姬專寵於內，昂等弄權於外，禍機竊發，有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: Lady Ma monopolizes favor within; Ang and others manipulate power without—omens of disaster secretly arise, more than can be told.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ma monopolizes favor within; Ang and others manipulate power without—omens of disaster secretly arise, more than can be told.

sentences.zh: 乞早誅以絕禍源。」

translations.literal: We beg early execution to cut off the source of calamity."
translations.idiomatic: We beg early execution to cut off the source of calamity.

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: Again no response.
translations.idiomatic: Again no response.

sentences.zh: 文華既數進直言，帝及諸近幸皆銜之。

translations.literal: Wenhua, having several times advanced straight speech, the Emperor and all the close favorites bore grudges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenhua, having several times advanced straight speech, the emperor and all the close favorites bore grudges against him.

sentences.zh: 會文華條上宗廟禮儀，祧廟、禘祫、特享、出主、祔食，凡五事。

translations.literal: When Wenhua itemized and submitted ancestral-temple ritual: ancestral shrines, di and cha offerings, special sacrifices, removal of spirit tablets, and attached feeding—in all five matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Wenhua itemized and submitted ancestral-temple ritual: ancestral shrines, di and cha offerings, special sacrifices, removal of spirit tablets, and attached feeding—in all five matters.

sentences.zh: 考證經義，悉可施行。

translations.literal: Investigating and verifying canonical meaning, all could be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating and verifying canonical meaning, all could be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責其出位妄言，章下所司。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged, rebuked him for speaking out of place in reckless words, and sent the memorial down to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, rebuked him for speaking out of place in reckless words, and sent the memorial down to the responsible office.

sentences.zh: 禮官暗於經術，又阿帝意，遂奏文華言非是。

translations.literal: The ritual officers were dark to canonical learning, and moreover curried the Emperor's intent, whereupon they memorialized that Wenhua's words were incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers were ignorant of canonical learning and, moreover, flattered the emperor's wishes; they then memorialized that Xu Wenhua's words were wrong.

sentences.zh: 命下詔獄，黜為民。

translations.literal: He was ordered into the imperial prison and demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the imperial prison and stripped of office, reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 時正德十一年十月也。

translations.literal: It was then the tenth month of the eleventh year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the tenth month of the eleventh year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，起故官，歷河南按察副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended, he was restored to his former office and served as Henan Surveillance Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor took the throne, Xu Wenhua was restored to his former rank and served as Henan Surveillance Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年舉治行卓異，入為大理右少卿，尋轉左。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was recommended for outstanding governance and entered office as Right Assistant Minister of Punishments at the Court of Revision, soon transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing he was recommended for outstanding governance, entered the capital as Right Assistant Minister of Punishments at the Court of Revision, and soon moved to the left post.

sentences.zh: 時方議興獻帝「大禮」，文華數偕諸大臣力爭。

translations.literal: At that time they were debating the "Great Rites" for Emperor Xian; Wenhua several times joined the great ministers in strenuous contention.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was debating the "Great Rites" for Emperor Xian; Xu Wenhua repeatedly joined the senior ministers in strenuous opposition.

sentences.zh: 明年七月復倡廷臣伏闕哭諫，坐停俸四月。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year he again led court officials to kneel weeping at the palace gate in remonstrance, for which his salary was suspended four months.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the following year he again led court officials to kneel and weep at the palace gate in remonstrance; his salary was suspended for four months.

sentences.zh: 已，席書、張璁、桂萼、方獻夫會廷臣大議，文華與汪偉、鄭嶽猶力爭。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xi Shu, Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu convened the court officials for a great debate; Wenhua together with Wang Wei and Zheng Yue still strove with all their might.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xi Shu, Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu convened the court for a great debate; Xu Wenhua, Wang Wei, and Zheng Yue still contested with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 武定侯郭勛遽曰：「祖訓如是，古禮如是，璁等言當。

translations.literal: Military Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun immediately said: "Ancestral instruction is thus, ancient ritual is thus—the words of Cong and the rest are correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, immediately said: "Ancestral instruction says so, ancient ritual says so—Cong and the others are right.

sentences.zh: 書曰大臣事君，當將順其美。」

translations.literal: The Book says that great ministers serving their lord should accommodate his excellence."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says that great ministers serving their ruler should accommodate his excellence.

sentences.zh: 議乃定。

translations.literal: The debate was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The debate was then settled.

sentences.zh: 及改題廟主，文華諫曰：「孝宗有祖道焉，不可以伯考稱。

translations.literal: When they changed the temple tablet inscriptions, Wenhua remonstrated, saying: "Emperor Xiaozong has the way of a grandfather—he cannot be called uncle-and-father.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple tablet inscriptions were changed, Xu Wenhua remonstrated: "Emperor Xiaozong stands in the way of a grandfather—he cannot be styled uncle-and-father.

sentences.zh: 武宗有父道焉，不可以兄稱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong has the way of a father—he cannot be called elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong stands in the way of a father—he cannot be styled elder brother.

sentences.zh: 不若直稱曰『孝宗敬皇帝』、『武宗毅皇帝』，猶兩全無害也。」

translations.literal: Better simply to call them "Emperor Xiaozong the Respectful" and "Emperor Wuzong the Resolute"—thus both are preserved without harm."
translations.idiomatic: Better simply to style them "Emperor Xiaozong the Respectful" and "Emperor Wuzong the Resolute"—that way both relationships are preserved without harm.

sentences.zh: 疏入，命再奪俸。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; he was ordered to lose salary again.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and he was ordered to forfeit salary again.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，李福達獄起。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year, the Li Fuda case arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year, the Li Fuda case broke out.

sentences.zh: 主獄者璁、萼、獻夫，以議禮故憾文華等，乃盡反獄詞，下文華與諸法官獄。

translations.literal: Those presiding over the case were Cong, E, and Xianfu; because of resentment over the ritual debate they fully reversed the case findings and sent Wenhua and the various judicial officials to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu presided over the case; resentful over the ritual debate, they fully reversed the findings and sent Xu Wenhua and the judicial officials to prison.

sentences.zh: 獄具，責文華阿附御史殺人，遣戍遼陽。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, they charged Wenhua with currying favor to help a censor commit murder and exiled him to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, they charged Xu Wenhua with currying favor to help a censor commit murder and exiled him to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，卒於道。

translations.literal: He encountered an amnesty but died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered an amnesty but died on the road.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈左僉都御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously given Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 自大學士毛紀、侍郎何孟春去位，諸大臣前爭「大禮」者，或依違順旨，文華顧堅守前議不變。

translations.literal: After Grand Secretary Mao Ji and Vice Minister He Mengchun left office, among the great ministers who had earlier contended over the "Great Rites," some wavered and complied with the imperial will, but Wenhua alone steadfastly held to his former position unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Secretary Mao Ji and Vice Minister He Mengchun left office, many ministers who had earlier fought over the "Great Rites" wavered and fell in with the imperial will; Xu Wenhua alone steadfastly held to his former position.

sentences.zh: 其被譴不以罪，士論深惜之。

translations.literal: His punishment was not for any crime—the opinion of the gentlemen deeply lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: His punishment was not for any crime, and scholarly opinion deeply lamented it.

sentences.zh: 薛蕙，字君采，亳州人。

translations.literal: Xue Hui, style Juncai, a native of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Hui, style Juncai, was a native of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 年十二能詩。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 舉正德九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he passed the advanced examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengde he passed the advanced examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 諫武宗南巡，受杖奪俸。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, was beaten with the rod and lost salary.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, was beaten with the rod, and lost his salary.

sentences.zh: 旋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起故官，改吏部，歷考功郎中。

translations.literal: Restored to his former office, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and rose to Director in the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to his former office, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and rose to Director in the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，廷臣數爭「大禮」，與張璁、桂萼等相持不下。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, court officials repeatedly contended over the "Great Rites," deadlocked with Zhang Cong, Gui E, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, court officials repeatedly contended over the "Great Rites," deadlocked with Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 蕙撰《為人後解》、《為人後辨》及辨璁、萼所論七事，合數萬言上於朝。

translations.literal: Hui composed the "Exposition on Becoming an Heir" and "Disputation on Becoming an Heir," and a refutation of seven points argued by Cong and E, totaling tens of thousands of words submitted to court.
translations.idiomatic: Hui composed the "Exposition on Becoming an Heir" and "Disputation on Becoming an Heir," together with a refutation of seven points argued by Cong and Gui E—tens of thousands of words in all—and submitted them to court.

sentences.zh: 《解》有上下二篇，推明大宗義。

translations.literal: The "Exposition" has upper and lower chapters, setting forth the meaning of the greater lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The "Exposition" has upper and lower chapters, setting forth the meaning of the greater lineage.

sentences.zh: 其《辨》曰：

translations.literal: His "Disputation" says:
translations.idiomatic: His "Disputation" reads:

sentences.zh: 陛下繼祖體而承嫡統，合於為人後之義，坦然無疑。

translations.literal: Your Majesty continues the ancestral body and undertakes the legitimate succession—this conforms to the meaning of becoming an heir, plainly without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty continues the ancestral body and undertakes the legitimate succession—this conforms to the meaning of becoming an heir, plainly and without doubt.

sentences.zh: 乃有二三臣者，詭經畔禮，上惑聖聰。

translations.literal: Yet one or two ministers distort the classics and betray ritual, unsettling the sage ear above.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one or two ministers distort the classics and betray ritual, unsettling Your Majesty's ear.

sentences.zh: 夫經傳纖悉之指，彼未能睹其十一，遽欲恃小慧，騁誇詞，可謂不知而作者也。

translations.literal: As for the subtle points of the classics and their commentaries, they have not seen one part in ten; yet they hasten to rely on petty wit and parade boastful words—this may be called composing while ignorant.
translations.idiomatic: As for the subtle points of the classics and their commentaries, they have scarcely grasped one part in ten; yet they hasten to rely on petty wit and parade boastful words—this may be called writing while ignorant.

sentences.zh: 其曰「陛下為獻帝不可奪之適嗣。」

translations.literal: They say, "Your Majesty is Emperor Xian's legitimate heir that cannot be taken away."
translations.idiomatic: They say, "Your Majesty is Emperor Xian's legitimate heir, and that status cannot be taken away."

sentences.zh: 按漢《石渠議》曰：「大宗無後，族無庶子，己有一適子，當絕父嗣以後大宗否？」

translations.literal: According to the Han Stone Canal Disputation: "The greater lineage has no heir; the clan has no secondary sons; one already has a legitimate son—should the father's succession be cut off to continue the greater lineage?"
translations.idiomatic: According to the Han Stone Canal Disputation: "The greater lineage has no heir; the clan has no secondary sons; one already has a legitimate son—should the father's succession be cut off to continue the greater lineage?"

sentences.zh: 戴聖云：「大宗不可絕。

translations.literal: Dai Sheng said: "The greater lineage cannot be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Sheng said: "The greater lineage cannot be cut off.

sentences.zh: 《禮》言適子不為後者，不得先庶子耳。

translations.literal: The Ritual says the legitimate son does not become an heir—this means he cannot take precedence over secondary sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual says the legitimate son does not become an heir—this means only that he cannot take precedence over secondary sons.

sentences.zh: 族無庶子，則當絕父以後大宗。」

translations.literal: If the clan has no secondary sons, then one should cut off the father to continue the greater lineage."
translations.idiomatic: If the clan has no secondary sons, then one should cut off the father to continue the greater lineage."

sentences.zh: 晉範汪曰：「廢小宗，昭穆不亂。

translations.literal: Jin's Fan Wang said: "To abolish the lesser lineage does not disorder the zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wang of Jin said: "To abolish the lesser lineage does not disorder the zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 廢大宗，昭穆亂矣。

translations.literal: To abolish the greater lineage disorders the zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: To abolish the greater lineage disorders the zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 先王所以重大宗也。

translations.literal: This is why the former kings so weightily esteemed the greater lineage.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the former kings so weightily esteemed the greater lineage.

sentences.zh: 豈得不廢小宗以繼大宗乎？」

translations.literal: How can one not abolish the lesser lineage to continue the greater lineage?"
translations.idiomatic: How can one not abolish the lesser lineage to continue the greater lineage?"

sentences.zh: 夫人子雖有適庶，其親親之心一也。

translations.literal: Though a son may have legitimate and secondary status, the heart that cherishes kin is one.
translations.idiomatic: Though a son may be legitimate or secondary, the heart that cherishes kin is one.

sentences.zh: 而《禮》適子不為後，庶子得為後者，此非親其父母有厚薄也，直系於傳重收族不同耳。

translations.literal: Yet in the Ritual the legitimate son does not become an heir while the secondary son may—this is not because love for one's parents is thick or thin; it stems directly from the difference in transmitting weight and gathering the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Ritual the legitimate son does not become an heir while the secondary son may—this is not because love for one's parents differs in depth; it stems directly from the difference in transmitting weight and gathering the clan.

sentences.zh: 今之言者不知推本祖禰，惟及其父母而止，此弗忍薄其親，忍遺其祖也。

translations.literal: Those who speak today do not know how to trace back to ancestors and forbears, but only reach as far as their parents and stop—this is unwillingness to slight one's kin, yet willingness to abandon one's ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak today do not know how to trace back to ancestors and forbears, but only reach as far as their parents and stop—unwilling to slight their kin, yet willing to abandon their ancestors.

sentences.zh: 其曰「為人後者為之子，乃漢儒邪說」。

translations.literal: They say, "One who becomes an heir becomes a son—this is Han Confucian heterodox talk."
translations.idiomatic: They say, "One who becomes an heir becomes a son—this is Han Confucian heterodox talk."

sentences.zh: 按此踵歐陽修之謬也。

translations.literal: According to this, it follows Ouyang Xiu's error.
translations.idiomatic: This follows in the footsteps of Ouyang Xiu's error.

sentences.zh: 夫「為人後者為之子」，其言出於《公羊》，固漢儒所傳者。

translations.literal: Now "one who becomes an heir becomes a son"—this saying comes from the Gongyang Commentary; it is indeed what Han scholars transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Now "one who becomes an heir becomes a son"—this saying comes from the Gongyang Commentary; it is indeed what Han scholars transmitted.

sentences.zh: 然於《儀禮》實相表裏，古今以為折衷，未有異論者也。

translations.literal: Yet in relation to the Ceremonies it is truly inner and outer; ancient and modern take it as the balanced view, and there has been no dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in relation to the Ceremonies it is truly inner and outer; ancient and modern take it as the balanced view, and there has been no dissent.

sentences.zh: 藉若修之說，其悖禮甚矣。

translations.literal: If we rely on Xiu's doctrine, its ritual transgression is very grave.
translations.idiomatic: If we rely on Xiu's doctrine, its transgression of ritual is very grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 《禮》「為人後者，斬衰三年」，此子於父母之喪也。

translations.literal: The Ritual: "One who becomes an heir wears cut sackcloth three years"—this is a son's mourning for parents.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual says, "One who becomes an heir wears cut sackcloth for three years"—this is a son's mourning for his parents.

sentences.zh: 以其父母之喪服之，非為之子而何？

translations.literal: To wear mourning for one's parents—is this not being a son?
translations.idiomatic: To wear mourning for one's parents as a son would—is this not being a son?

sentences.zh: 其言之悖禮一也。

translations.literal: This is the first way their words transgress ritual.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first way their words transgress ritual.

sentences.zh: 傳言「為所後者之祖父母妻，妻之父母昆弟，昆弟之子若子」。

translations.literal: The commentary says "for the grandparents, wife, wife's parents, brothers, and brothers' sons of one succeeded—if sons."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, "for the grandparents, wife, wife's parents, brothers, and brothers' sons of the one succeeded—as if sons."

sentences.zh: 其若子者，由為之子故耳。

translations.literal: The "if sons" is because one has become a son.
translations.idiomatic: The "as if sons" is because one has become a son.

sentences.zh: 傳明言「若子」，今顧曰「不為之子」，其言之悖禮二也。

translations.literal: The commentary plainly says "if sons," yet they now say "does not become a son"—this is the second ritual transgression.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary plainly says "as if sons," yet they now say "does not become a son"—this is the second ritual transgression.

sentences.zh: 且為人後者不為之子，然則稱謂之間，將不曰父，而仍曰伯父、叔父乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, if one who becomes an heir does not become a son, then in terms of address would one not say father but still say uncle and father's younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if one who becomes an heir does not become a son, then in address would one not say father but still say uncle and father's younger brother?

sentences.zh: 其言之悖禮三也。

translations.literal: This is the third ritual transgression.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third ritual transgression.

sentences.zh: 又立後而不為之子，則古立後者，皆未嘗實子之，而姑偽立是人也。

translations.literal: Further, to establish an heir yet not make him a son—then all who in antiquity established heirs never truly made them sons, but merely pretended to set up such a person.
translations.idiomatic: Further, to establish an heir yet not make him a son would mean that all who in antiquity established heirs never truly made them sons, but merely pretended to set up such a person.

sentences.zh: 是聖人偽教人以立後，而實則無後焉耳。

translations.literal: Then the sage falsely taught people to establish heirs while in reality there were no heirs at all.
translations.idiomatic: Then the sage falsely taught people to establish heirs while in reality there were no heirs at all.

sentences.zh: 其言之悖禮四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth ritual transgression.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth ritual transgression.

sentences.zh: 夫無後者，重絕祖考之祀，故立後以奉之。

translations.literal: Now those without heirs weightily sever sacrifices to ancestors and forebears; therefore heirs are established to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Those without heirs weightily sever sacrifices to ancestors and forebears; therefore heirs are established to serve them.

sentences.zh: 今所後既不得而子，則祖考亦不得而孫矣。

translations.literal: If the one succeeded cannot become a son, then ancestors and forebears also cannot gain grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: If the one succeeded cannot become a son, then ancestors and forebears also cannot gain grandsons.

sentences.zh: 豈可以入其廟而奉其祀乎？

translations.literal: How can one enter their temple and tend their sacrifices?
translations.idiomatic: How can one enter their temple and tend their sacrifices?

sentences.zh: 其言之悖禮五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth ritual transgression.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth ritual transgression.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，名漢臣以邪說，無乃其自名耶？

translations.literal: Viewed thus, to call Han ministers heterodox talk—is it not rather naming themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, to call Han ministers heterodox—is it not rather naming themselves?

sentences.zh: 抑二三臣者亦自度其說之必窮也，於是又為遁辭以倡之曰：「夫統與嗣不同，陛下之繼二宗，當繼統而不繼嗣。」

translations.literal: Yet those one or two ministers also measured that their doctrine must come to an end; therefore they again devised evasive words to advocate: "Line and succession differ—Your Majesty's continuing two lineages should continue the line but not the succession."
translations.idiomatic: Yet those one or two ministers also saw that their doctrine must come to an end; therefore they devised evasive words to advocate: "Line and succession differ—Your Majesty's continuing two lineages should continue the line but not the succession.

sentences.zh: 此一言者，將欲以廢先王為人後之義與？

translations.literal: This single saying—does it intend to abolish the former kings' meaning of becoming an heir?
translations.idiomatic: Does this single saying intend to abolish the former kings' meaning of becoming an heir?

sentences.zh: 則尤悖禮之甚者也。

translations.literal: Then it is ritual transgression in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Then it is ritual transgression in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 然其牽合附會，眩於名實，茍不辨而絕之，殆將為後世禍矣。

translations.literal: Yet their forced alignments and specious unions dazzle regarding names and realities; if not distinguished and cut off, they will nearly become calamity for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their forced alignments and specious unions dazzle regarding names and realities; if not distinguished and cut off, they will nearly become calamity for later generations.

sentences.zh: 夫《禮》為大宗立後者，重其統也。

translations.literal: Now the Ritual establishes heirs for the greater lineage because it weights their line.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual establishes heirs for the greater lineage because it weights their line.

sentences.zh: 重其統不可絕，乃為之立後。

translations.literal: Because the line cannot be cut off, heirs are established for it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the line cannot be cut off, heirs are established for it.

sentences.zh: 至於小宗不為之後者，統可以絕，則嗣可以不繼也。

translations.literal: As for the lesser lineage, for which heirs are not established—the line may be cut off, so succession need not continue.
translations.idiomatic: As for the lesser lineage, for which heirs are not established—the line may be cut off, so succession need not continue.

sentences.zh: 是則以繼統故繼嗣，繼嗣所以繼統也。

translations.literal: Thus one continues succession because of continuing the line; continuing succession is how one continues the line.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one continues succession because of continuing the line; continuing succession is how one continues the line.

sentences.zh: 故《禮》「為人後」，言繼嗣也；

translations.literal: Therefore in the Ritual "becoming an heir" speaks of continuing succession;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the Ritual "becoming an heir" speaks of continuing succession;

sentences.zh: 「後大宗」，言繼統也。

translations.literal: "succeeding the greater lineage" speaks of continuing the line.
translations.idiomatic: "succeeding the greater lineage" speaks of continuing the line.

sentences.zh: 統與嗣，非有二也，其何不同之有？

translations.literal: Line and succession are not two things—what difference can there be?
translations.idiomatic: Line and succession are not two things—what difference can there be?

sentences.zh: 自古帝王入繼者，必明為人後之義，而後可以繼統。

translations.literal: From antiquity, emperors and kings who entered succession must clearly clarify the meaning of becoming an heir, and only then can they continue the line.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, emperors and kings who entered succession must clearly clarify the meaning of becoming an heir, and only then can they continue the line.

sentences.zh: 蓋不為後則不成子也。

translations.literal: For if one does not become an heir, one does not become a son.
translations.idiomatic: For if one does not become an heir, one does not become a son.

sentences.zh: 若不成子，夫安所得統而繼之。

translations.literal: If one does not become a son, how can one obtain the line to continue it.
translations.idiomatic: If one does not become a son, how can one obtain the line to continue it.

sentences.zh: 故為後也者，成子也，成子而後繼統，又將以絕同宗覬覦之心焉。

translations.literal: Therefore becoming an heir means becoming a son; becoming a son and then continuing the line also removes the hearts of the same clan that covet and gaze upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore becoming an heir means becoming a son; becoming a son and then continuing the line also removes the covetous hearts of the same clan.

sentences.zh: 聖人之制禮也，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: When the sage fashioned ritual, was it not excellent.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage fashioned ritual, was it not excellent.

sentences.zh: 抑成子而後繼統，非獨為人後者爾也。

translations.literal: Yet becoming a son and then continuing the line is not only for those who become heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet becoming a son and then continuing the line is not only for those who become heirs.

sentences.zh: 《禮》無生而貴者。

translations.literal: The Ritual has no one noble by birth alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual recognizes no one as noble by birth alone.

sentences.zh: 雖天子諸侯之子，茍不受命於君父，亦不敢自成尊也。

translations.literal: Even the sons of the Son of Heaven and feudal lords—if they do not receive command from lord and father, they dare not make themselves honored of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Even the sons of the Son of Heaven and feudal lords—if they do not receive command from lord and father, they dare not make themselves honored on their own.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》重授受之義，以為為子受之父，為臣受之君。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals weights the meaning of receiving and transmitting—it holds that as son one receives from father, as minister one receives from lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals weights the meaning of receiving and transmitting—it holds that as son one receives from father, as minister one receives from lord.

sentences.zh: 故穀梁子曰「臣子必受君父之命」。

translations.literal: Therefore Master Guliang said "minister and son must receive the lord and father's command."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Master Guliang said, "Minister and son must receive the lord and father's command."

sentences.zh: 斯義也，非直尊君父也，亦所以自尊焉耳。

translations.literal: This meaning is not only honoring lord and father—it is also how one honors oneself.
translations.idiomatic: This meaning is not only honoring lord and father—it is also how one honors oneself.

sentences.zh: 蓋尊其君父，亦將使人之尊己也。

translations.literal: For honoring one's lord and father will also make others honor oneself.
translations.idiomatic: For honoring one's lord and father will also make others honor oneself.

sentences.zh: 如此則義禮明而禍亂亡。

translations.literal: Thus ritual and righteousness are clear and calamity and chaos are extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus righteousness and ritual are clear, and calamity and chaos are extinguished.

sentences.zh: 今說者謂『倫序當立斯立已』，是惡知《禮》與《春秋》之意哉！

translations.literal: Now the advocates say "when ritual order demands establishment, establish immediately"—how can they know the intent of the Ritual and Spring and Autumn Annals!
translations.idiomatic: Now the advocates say, "When ritual order demands establishment, establish it at once"—how can they know the intent of the Ritual and the Spring and Autumn Annals!

sentences.zh: 若夫前代之君，間有弟終而兄繼，侄終而伯叔父繼者，此遭變不正者也。

translations.literal: As for rulers of former dynasties, occasionally when a younger brother died and an elder brother succeeded, or a nephew died and an uncle succeeded—this was encountering irregularity, not the correct case.
translations.idiomatic: As for rulers of former dynasties, occasionally when a younger brother died and an elder brother succeeded, or a nephew died and an uncle succeeded—this was encountering irregularity, not the correct case.

sentences.zh: 然多先君之嗣。

translations.literal: Yet mostly there were sons of the former lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mostly there were sons of the former lord.

sentences.zh: 先君於己則考也，己於先君則子也。

translations.literal: The former lord toward oneself is "father"; oneself toward the former lord is "son."
translations.idiomatic: The former lord toward oneself is "father"; oneself toward the former lord is "son."

sentences.zh: 故不可考後君，而亦無兩統二父之嫌，若晉之哀帝、唐之宣宗是也。

translations.literal: Therefore one cannot treat the later lord as "father," and there is no suspicion of two lines and two fathers—as with Jin's Emperor Ai and Tang's Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one cannot treat the later lord as "father," and there is no suspicion of two lines and two fathers—as with Jin's Emperor Ai and Tang's Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 其或諸王入嗣，則未有仍考諸王而不考天子者也。

translations.literal: Or when various princes entered succession, there has never been still treating the various princes as "father" while not treating the Son of Heaven as "father."
translations.idiomatic: Or when various princes entered succession, there has never been still treating the princes as "father" while not treating the Son of Heaven as "father."

sentences.zh: 陛下天倫不先於武宗，正統不自於獻帝，是非予奪，至為易辨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heavenly kin is not prior to Emperor Wuzong; legitimate succession does not originate from Emperor Xian—right and wrong, grant and withhold, are extremely easy to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heavenly kin is not prior to Emperor Wuzong; legitimate succession does not originate from Emperor Xian—right and wrong, grant and withhold, are extremely easy to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 而二三臣者猥欲比於遭變不正之舉，故曰悖禮之尤者也。

translations.literal: Yet those one or two ministers basely wished to compare with irregular successions of the past—therefore they are called ritual transgression in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those one or two ministers basely wished to compare with irregular successions of the past—therefore they are called ritual transgression in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 其他所辨七事，亦率仿此。

translations.literal: The other seven matters he argued likewise generally imitated this.
translations.idiomatic: His rebuttals on the other seven points followed much the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 書奏，天子大怒，下鎮撫司考訊。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven was greatly enraged and sent him down to the Brocade Guard prison for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor flew into a rage and had him sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 已，貰出之，奪俸三月。

translations.literal: Before long he was pardoned and released; his salary was withheld for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was pardoned and released, though his salary was withheld for three months.

sentences.zh: 會給事中陳洸外轉，疑事由文選郎夏良勝及蕙。

translations.literal: It happened that when Supervising Secretary Chen Guang was transferred outward, he suspected the matter was due to Document Selection Clerk Xia Liangsheng and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: About then Supervising Secretary Chen Guang was posted away from the capital; he suspected the affair was the work of Document Selection Clerk Xia Liangsheng and Hui.

sentences.zh: 良勝已被訐見斥，而蕙故在。

translations.literal: Liangsheng had already been impeached and dismissed, while Hui remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liangsheng had already been impeached and dismissed, but Hui still held his post.

sentences.zh: 時亳州知州顏木方坐罪，乃誣蕙與木同年相關通，疑有奸利。

translations.literal: At the time Bozhou Prefect Yan Mu had just been convicted of a crime; he then falsely accused Hui of colluding with Mu as fellow examination-year mates, suspecting corrupt profit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bozhou Prefect Yan Mu had just been convicted; he falsely accused Hui of colluding with Mu as men of the same examination year, alleging illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 章下所司，蕙亦奏辨。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office; Hui also submitted a memorial in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The accusation was referred to the appropriate office, and Hui submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，令解任聽勘。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen and ordered him to leave his post pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear him out and ordered him to resign his post pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 蕙遂南歸。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then returned to the south.

sentences.zh: 既而事白，吏部數移文促蕙起。

translations.literal: Before long the matter was cleared; the Ministry of Personnel repeatedly sent official letters urging Hui to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the matter was cleared, and the Ministry of Personnel sent repeated dispatches urging Hui to return to office.

sentences.zh: 蕙見璁、萼等用事，堅臥不肯起。

translations.literal: Hui saw Cong, E, and others wielding power and steadfastly lay abed, refusing to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Cong, E, and their faction in power, Hui steadfastly remained in retirement and refused to return.

sentences.zh: 十八年詔選宮僚，擬蕙春坊司直兼翰林檢討。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year an edict selected palace tutors and proposed Hui as Instructor in the Eastern Palace, concurrently as Hanlin Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing an edict called for palace tutors; Hui was proposed as Instructor in the Eastern Palace, concurrently as Hanlin Reviser.

sentences.zh: 帝猶以前憾故，報罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor, still because of the earlier grudge, returned the proposal disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still nursing the old grievance, returned the nomination disapproved.

sentences.zh: 而蕙亦卒矣。

translations.literal: And Hui also died.
translations.idiomatic: And Hui died as well.

sentences.zh: 蕙貌臒氣清，持己峻潔，於書無所不讀。

translations.literal: Hui's appearance was gaunt and his bearing clear; he held himself stern and pure, and among books there was none he did not read.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was gaunt in appearance and lucid in manner; he held himself to a stern purity and read every book he could find.

sentences.zh: 學者重其學行，稱為「西原先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars prized his learning and conduct and called him "Master Xiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honored his learning and conduct and called him Master Xiyuan.

sentences.zh: 當是時，廷臣力持「大禮」，而璁、萼建異議，舉朝非之。

translations.literal: At that time court ministers forcefully upheld the "Great Rites," while Cong and E raised dissenting views, and the whole court disapproved of them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court ministers forcefully upheld the Great Rites, while Zhang Cong and Gui E pressed contrary views that the whole court rejected.

sentences.zh: 其不獲與廷議，而以璁、萼得罪者，又有胡侍、王祿、侯廷訓雲。

translations.literal: Those who could not join court deliberation yet were punished on account of Cong and E included Hu Shi, Wang Lu, and Hou Tingxun, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Others who could not join the court debate yet suffered for opposing Cong and E included Hu Shi, Wang Lu, and Hou Tingxun, among others.

sentences.zh: 胡侍，寧夏人。

translations.literal: Hu Shi was a native of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shi was from Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 歷官鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Minister of Ceremonial Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Ceremonial Reception.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼既擢學士，侍劾二人越禮背經。

translations.literal: After Zhang Cong and Gui E were promoted to Academicians, Shi memorialized impeaching the two for overstepping ritual and opposing the classics.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Cong and Gui E were promoted to Hanlin Academicians, Shi memorialized impeaching them for overstepping ritual and defying the classics.

sentences.zh: 因據所奏，反復論辨，凡千余言。

translations.literal: Drawing on their submitted positions, he argued back and forth, in all more than a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on their own submissions, he argued the case back and forth in more than a thousand words.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命逮治。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and ordered him arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 言官論救，謫潞州同知。

translations.literal: Censorial officials argued in his defense; he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials pleaded for him, and he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 沈府宗室勛註以事憾之，奏侍試諸生題譏刺，且謗「大禮」。

translations.literal: A Shen-household clansman, Xun Zhu, bore him a grudge over a matter and memorialized that Shi, in setting examination topics for students, had used satirical wording and also slandered the "Great Rites."
translations.idiomatic: A clansman of the Prince of Shen, Xun Zhu, bore him a grudge over an affair and memorialized that Shi had set examination topics for students that were satirical and had also slandered the Great Rites.

sentences.zh: 逮至京，訊斥為民。

translations.literal: He was arrested and brought to the capital; after interrogation he was stripped of office and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and brought to the capital; after interrogation he was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 王祿，新城人。

translations.literal: Wang Lu was a native of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lu was from Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，為福建平和知縣。

translations.literal: Having passed the provincial examination, he served as magistrate of Pinghe in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the provincial examination, he served as magistrate of Pinghe in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，疏請建獻帝廟於安陸，封崇仁王以主其祀，不當考獻帝，伯孝宗，涉二本之嫌。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing he memorialized asking to build a temple to Emperor Xian at Anlu, enfeoff the Prince of Chongren to preside over the sacrifices, that one should not treat Xian as father in the rites, but treat Xiaozong as elder uncle, involving the suspicion of two fathers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 he memorialized asking that a temple to Emperor Xian be built at Anlu and the Prince of Chongren be enfeoffed to preside over the sacrifices; that the emperor should not treat Xian as his father in the rites but Xiaozong as his uncle, avoiding the taint of two fathers.

sentences.zh: 宗藩子有幼而岐嶷者，當養之宮中，備儲貳選。

translations.literal: Princely sons of the imperial clan who in youth show precocious ability should be reared in the palace as reserve candidates for heir selection.
translations.idiomatic: Princely sons of the imperial clan who show precocious ability in youth should be reared in the palace as reserve candidates for the succession.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，即棄官歸。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he immediately abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the memorial was in, he resigned his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 命按臣逮治，亦斥為民。

translations.literal: He was ordered arrested and tried by an investigating commissioner; he too was stripped and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: An investigating commissioner was ordered to arrest and try him; he too was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 侯廷訓，樂清人。

translations.literal: Hou Tingxun was a native of Yueqing.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tingxun was from Yueqing.

sentences.zh: 與張璁同郡，同舉進士，而持論不合。

translations.literal: He was from the same prefecture as Zhang Cong and passed the metropolitan examination the same year, but their views did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same prefecture as Zhang Cong and passed the metropolitan examination in the same year, but their views did not agree.

sentences.zh: 初釋褐，即上疏請考孝宗，且言不當私藩邸舊臣，語最切直。

translations.literal: As soon as he left the dyed robe—that is, upon first taking office—he memorialized asking to treat Xiaozong as father in the rites and also said one must not favor old retainers of the princely residence; his language was most trenchant.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he entered office he memorialized asking that Xiaozong be treated as his father in the rites and declared that one must not show favor to old retainers of the princely residence; his language was trenchant in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 除南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Principal Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年冬，「大禮」定，廷訓心非之。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year of Jiajing, when the "Great Rites" were settled, Tingxun inwardly opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Jiajing 3, when the Great Rites were settled, Tingxun inwardly rejected the outcome.

sentences.zh: 私刊所著議禮書，潛寄京師，下詔獄拷訊。

translations.literal: He privately printed his book debating the ritual question and secretly sent it to the capital; he was sent to the imperial prison for torture interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He privately printed his book on the ritual debate and secretly sent copies to the capital; he was sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture.

sentences.zh: 子一元，年十三，伏闕訟冤，得釋。

translations.literal: His son Yiyuan, aged thirteen, prostrated himself at the palace gate to plead the injustice, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiyuan, aged thirteen, prostrated himself at the palace gate to plead his father's innocence, and Tingxun was released.

sentences.zh: 後起官至漳南僉事。

translations.literal: Later reappointed, he rose to Assistant Administration Commissioner of Southern Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later reappointed, he rose to Assistant Administration Commissioner of Southern Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以貪虐，被劾為民。

translations.literal: For greed and cruelty he was impeached and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: For greed and cruelty he was impeached and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 一元舉進士，官至江西布政使。

translations.literal: Yiyuan passed the metropolitan examination and rose to Administrative Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan passed the metropolitan examination and rose to Administrative Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「大禮」之議，楊廷和為之倡，舉朝翕然同聲，大抵本宋司馬光、程頤《濮園議》。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the debate over the "Great Rites," Yang Tinghe took the lead; the whole court joined in unanimous voice—broadly it rested on Song Sima Guang's and Cheng Yi's "Memorial on the Puyi Garden."
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the debate over the Great Rites, Yang Tinghe led the way and the whole court spoke as one—broadly following Sima Guang and Cheng Yi's Memorial on the Puyi Garden from the Song.

sentences.zh: 然英宗長育宮中，名稱素定。

translations.literal: Yet Yingzong was raised long in the palace, and his title and status were long since settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in that case Yingzong had been raised in the palace from childhood, and his title and status were long settled.

sentences.zh: 而世宗奉詔嗣位，承武宗後，事勢各殊。

translations.literal: But Shizong succeeded by edict, continuing after Wuzong—the circumstances were wholly different.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, by contrast, succeeded by edict and continued the line after Wuzong—the circumstances were wholly different.

sentences.zh: 諸臣徒見先賢大儒成說可據，求無得罪天下後世，而未暇為世宗熟計審處，準酌情理，以求至當。

translations.literal: The ministers only saw that established pronouncements of ancient worthies and great Confucians could be cited, seeking to avoid offending the world and posterity, yet had no leisure to plan carefully and weigh for Shizong, calibrating feeling and principle to reach what was most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers saw only that the settled pronouncements of ancient worthies and great Confucians could be cited, and sought to avoid offending the world and posterity; they had no leisure to think through Shizong's case carefully, weigh feeling against principle, and arrive at what was truly fitting.

sentences.zh: 爭之愈力，失之愈深，惜夫。

translations.literal: The more forcefully they disputed, the deeper the error—alas.
translations.idiomatic: The harder they fought, the further they strayed—a pity indeed.
